questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Animal rights activists were protesting the use of monkeys in medical experiments by scientists who were developing a vaccine for a harmful virus. For several consecutive days, the activists marched in front of the exit door of the scientists' laboratory so that the scientists could not leave without first facing a barrage of name-calling and heckling from the activists. One scientist who was particularly agitated by the protesting decided to take revenge on one of the most vocal activists. On her way out of the laboratory, the scientist threw the skull of a monkey at the activist. The activist happened to turn his body and look away just after the scientist threw the skull. The skull struck the bag that the activist was carrying on his back. Upon discovering that he had been hit by a monkey skull, the activist became extremely distressed and upset.
Is the scientist guilty of the crime of battery?

choices.A: No, because the activist did not see the monkey skull coming toward him.
choices.B: No, because the monkey skull struck the activist's backpack instead of his person.
choices.C: Yes, because the scientist had the specific intent to throw the monkey skull at the activist.
choices.D: Yes, because there was an unlawful application of force that constituted an offensive touching.

questions.explanation:
Criminal Battery

(application of force to another’s person)

Unlawful force
Object near victim
Bodily harm
Unlawful force
Object attached
to victim
Offensive touching

Criminal battery is the unlawful application of force to the victim's person—including an object near, carried by, or attached to the victim—that causes bodily harm or constitutes an offensive touching. Contact is offensive if a reasonable person would find it unpleasant or repugnant.

Here, the scientist unlawfully threw a monkey skull (unlawful application of force) at the activist, striking the backpack that the activist was carrying (victim's person). Being struck by a monkey skull would be unpleasant or repugnant to a reasonable person, so the resulting contact was offensive. Therefore, the scientist is guilty of criminal battery (Choice D).

(Choice A) Unlike assault, which arises from an attempted battery or when a defendant intentionally places another in reasonable apprehension of imminent contact, battery does not require proof of apprehension. Therefore, the fact that the activist did not see the monkey skull coming is irrelevant.

(Choice C) Battery is a general intent crime, so the criminal act (throwing a skull) need only be consciously performed or criminally negligent. Therefore, the scientist's specific intent—ie, that the criminal act be performed for a particular purpose (to hit the activist)—is not required to find her guilty of battery.

📌 Educational Objective

Criminal battery is the unlawful application of force to the victim's person—including an object near, carried by, or attached to the victim—that causes bodily harm or constitutes an offensive touching.
questions.zh-question:
动物权利活动家们正在抗议科学家在研发一种有害病毒疫苗时使用猴子进行医学实验。连续几天，活动家们在科学家实验室的出口门前游行，导致科学家们在离开前不得不面对活动家们的谩骂和诘难。一位被抗议活动特别激怒的科学家决定报复其中一名叫嚣最凶的活动家。在离开实验室的路上，这位科学家将一个猴子头骨扔向了那名活动家。就在科学家扔出头骨后，那名活动家恰好转身并看向别处。头骨击中了活动家背着的包。当发现自己被猴子头骨击中后，这名活动家变得极度痛苦和不安。

该科学家是否犯有伤害罪（battery）？

zh-choices.A: 不构成，因为活动家没有看到猴子头骨向他飞来。
zh-choices.B: 不构成，因为猴子头骨击中的是活动家的背包，而不是他的人身。
zh-choices.C: 构成，因为科学家有将猴子头骨扔向活动家的特定意图。
zh-choices.D: 构成，因为存在非法使用武力，构成了冒犯性接触。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes Against the Person

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：刑事 battery（殴击罪） 是否成立，关键看被告是否对受害人本人或其随身物品实施了 unlawful application of force（非法用力），并造成 offensive touching（令人反感的接触）。

三秒认题路径：

扔猴骨 → 打到背包 → 随身物品算人身 → 令人反感接触 → 选 D

核心法律规则

Battery（殴击罪） 的考试意思：只要被告故意或至少不法地把力加在受害人person（人身）上，就可能成立；这个“人身”不仅包括身体，也包括受害人carried by（随身携带） 或 attached to（附着） 的物品。Offensive touching（令人反感的接触） 的考试意思：站在一般理性人角度觉得不舒服、冒犯、恶心，就够了，不需要真的造成重伤。这里猴骨打到受害人背包，背包是他随身携带的东西，所以仍然算打到“人身”，且对普通人来说明显令人反感。

核心判例： 本题对应的是普通法 battery 规则，不靠伤口大小，重点是对受害人本人或其随身物品的非法接触。

思维导图

先看：这是终局伤害吗？
是本题答案路径：不是在问人受没受伤多重，而是在问有没有对“人身”造成非法接触。
再看：接触打到哪里？
事实钩子：猴骨没有打到脸或手，但打中了受害人背着的背包。
关键关卡：背包算不算“受害人的人身”？
算。随身携带的物品被打到，也属于 battery 的用力对象。
最后落点：接触是否令人反感？
当然是：被猴骨击中背包，对一般理性人足以构成 offensive touching（令人反感的接触）。
结论 →
答案：科学家构成 criminal battery（刑事殴击罪），选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想： 受害人没看到猴骨飞来，而且骨头只打到背包，不是打到身体，所以不算 battery。

但考试真正问的是： battery（殴击罪） 不要求受害人事先察觉，也不要求直接打到皮肤；打到他随身携带的背包，同样可能成立。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里 猴骨击中受害人背着的背包，背包算受害人的随身物品，属于对人身的非法用力，所以构成 offensive touching。

❌ 概念混淆 | 误把 assault 当 battery

✕ A: 把 did not see 当成关键，但 battery 不看事前是否看见。

❌ 事实误判 | 偷换接触位置

✕ B: 误把“打到背包”说成没打到人，随身携带物品本来就算。

❌ 法律适用 | 误用特定意图

✕ C: 把 specific intent 硬塞进 battery，但这里看的是一般故意或非法用力。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定是否对“受害人的人身”用力，再看被打到的是不是其随身物品。

考场速记

记住：battery（殴击罪） 先问“有没有非法接触到受害人的人身或随身物品”，再问“这接触对一般人是否令人反感”。猴骨打到背包也算打到人，别被“没碰到身体”骗走。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A woman drove her car through the drive-through lane of a fast-food restaurant one afternoon. When she reached the microphone used to place orders, she said, "There's a man across the street with a rifle. He can see everything you do. If you do not do exactly what I tell you, he will shoot you. Put all the money from the register into a sack and give it to me when I drive up." The clerk did not see anyone across the street and was unsure whether anyone was there. However, unwilling to risk harm to himself, he put $500 in a paper bag and handed it to the woman when she drove up to the delivery window. The woman drove off with the money but was arrested a short time later. She had lied about there having been a man with a rifle and had acted alone.
What is the most serious crime of which the woman can be convicted?

choices.A: Embezzlement.
choices.B: False pretenses.
choices.C: Larceny.
choices.D: Robbery.

questions.explanation:
Robbery
(larceny by force v. intimidation)
Force Use of more force than necessary to acquire property or retain the property immediately thereafter
Intimidation Threat that places victim in reasonable apprehension of immediate death or serious physical injury to victim, close family member, or person present

Larceny is (1) the unlawful taking and carrying away of the victim's personal property (2) with the specific intent to permanently deprive the victim of that property. And larceny becomes robbery when:

  • the property is taken from the victim's person or presence and
  • the taking is accomplished by force or intimidation.

Since larceny is necessarily committed during robbery, it is a lesser included offense of robbery. And under the merger doctrine, a defendant can only be convicted of larceny (lesser offense) or robbery (greater offense).

Here, the woman committed larceny when she took $500 from the clerk and drove away. But she acquired the money by threatening to have the clerk immediately shot if he did not comply. And since the clerk gave her the money because he was unwilling to risk being harmed, the woman can be convicted of the more serious crime of robbery (Choice C).

(Choice A) Embezzlement occurs when a person in lawful possession of another's property fraudulently converts it. Since the woman took unlawful possession of the money, she cannot be convicted of embezzlement.

(Choice B) False pretenses requires proof that the defendant (1) knowingly misrepresented a past or existing material fact (2) with the intent to defraud and (3) thereby obtained title to another's property. Here, the woman lied to the clerk when she said that a man with a rifle was ready to shoot him. But since the woman never obtained title to the money, she cannot be convicted of false pretenses.

📌 Educational Objective

Larceny becomes robbery when property is taken from the victim's person or presence by force or intimidation. Since larceny merges into the completed robbery, a defendant can be convicted of either crime—but not both.
questions.zh-question:
一天下午，一名女子驾车通过一家快餐店的“得来速”车道。当她到达点餐用的麦克风时，她说：“街对面有个男人拿着步枪。他能看到你做的一切。如果你不完全按照我说的做，他就会开枪射你。把收银机里所有的钱都放进一个袋子里，等我开车过来时给我。”店员没有看到街对面有任何人，也不确定是否有人在那里。然而，由于不愿让自己冒受伤害的风险，他将500美元放进一个纸袋，在该女子开车到取餐窗口时交给了她。该女子带着钱开车离开，但不久后被捕。她谎称有持步枪的男子，且是单独行动。

该女子可能被定罪的最严重罪行是什么？

zh-choices.A: 侵占罪 (Embezzlement)。
zh-choices.B: 诈欺罪 (False pretenses)。
zh-choices.C: 盗窃罪 (Larceny)。
zh-choices.D: 抢劫罪 (Robbery)。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：抢劫（robbery）是不是由 盗窃（larceny） 加上 威胁/恐吓（intimidation） 升级而来。

三秒认题路径：

先看拿钱 → 再看威胁 → 物在身边 → 直接给钱 → 选抢劫

核心法律规则

盗窃（larceny）是未经同意拿走他人动产，并带着 永久剥夺（intent to permanently deprive） 的意思。抢劫（robbery）就是把盗窃做在 受害人本人或其在场范围（person or presence） 内，而且是靠 暴力（force） 或 恐吓（intimidation） 完成，所以考场意思就是：钱虽然是自己拿走的，但如果是靠“现在就会出事”的威胁逼对方交出来，罪名会从盗窃升级成抢劫。

这里的 intimidation（恐吓）考场意思：让被害人合理地担心自己会立刻遭到严重伤害。只要被害人是因为怕马上被打/被枪击才交钱，robbery 就成立。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用；本题的控制规则来自普通法抢劫定义：盗窃 + 人身/在场 + 暴力或恐吓。

思维导图

先问：拿钱是不是靠“现在会出事”的威胁？
是 对着店员说：
有持枪的人
在监视你 → 店员因恐惧
把钱交出来 → 盗窃成立 + 恐吓完成 → 结论：抢劫（robbery）
别被骗 不是在问
有没有真的枪手 → 而是在问
店员是不是被迫交钱 → 所以答案选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她只是撒谎骗钱，听起来像 false pretenses 或 larceny。

但考试真正问的是：店员是不是因为“马上会被枪击”的威胁才交钱；一旦答案是“是”，就不是单纯骗取，而是 robbery。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的关键点是 威胁立刻开枪，店员因恐惧把钱交出，所以这是 robbery，不是单纯偷拿。

❌ 概念混淆 | 占有性质误判

✕ A: 她不是先合法占有再挪用，别把 lawful possession 套进来。

❌ 法律适用 | 取得所有权误判

✕ B: 她只是把钱逼到手，没在骗店员把 title 转给她。

❌ 事实误判 | 误把取钱当终局

✕ C: 题干最狠的是当场威胁，不是悄悄拿走财物。

这题建议用什么方法？

先盯“钱怎么出来的”，只要是靠即时恐吓逼出来的，就优先往抢劫走。

考场速记

记住一句：抢劫 = 盗窃 + 当场暴力/恐吓。看到“我马上开枪/你现在就会受伤”这类话，就先想抢劫，再排除别的财产罪。In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 这类口诀是程序题用的；本题不用背，真正要背的是“人就在场、钱是被吓出来的”。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
After waiting until all the customers had left, a man entered a small grocery store just before closing time. He went up to the lone clerk in the store and said, "Hand over all the money in the cash register or you will get hurt." The clerk fainted and struck his head on the edge of the counter. As the man went behind the counter to open the cash register, two customers entered the store. The man ran out before he was able to open the register drawer.
Of which crime(s) could the man be properly convicted based on this evidence?

choices.A: Assault and attempted robbery.
choices.B: Assault and robbery.
choices.C: Attempted robbery.
choices.D: Robbery.

questions.explanation:
Robbery
(greater offense)
Larceny (lesser offense)
  • Unlawful taking & carrying away of victim’s property
  • Specific intent to permanently deprive
+
Battery (lesser offense)
  • force used to cause bodily injury or offensive touching
OR
Assault (lesser offense)
  • attempted battery or conduct causing apprehension of
    imminent harm

Robbery requires proof of all of the following elements:

  • The defendant unlawfully took and carried away the victim's personal property.
  • The property was taken from the victim's person or presence by force or intimidation (eg, assault).
  • The defendant specifically intended to permanently deprive the victim of the property (ie, to steal).

But a defendant who does not complete all of these elements can still be convicted of attempted robbery if he/she (1) had the specific intent to commit robbery and (2) committed an act in furtherance of that crime.

Here, the man did not commit robbery since he ran out of the store before he could take the money (Choices B & D). But since he specifically intended to steal the cash by intimidation and committed an act in furtherance of the robbery when he threatened to hurt the clerk, he can be convicted of attempted robbery.

Assault is (1) an attempted battery or (2) conduct that intentionally puts the victim in reasonable apprehension of imminent bodily harm. Therefore, the man committed assault in the course of the attempted robbery when he threatened to hurt the clerk if he did not comply. But since assault satisfies the intimidation requirement for robbery, it is a lesser included offense. As a result, the assault merges with the attempted or completed robbery. This means that the man can be convicted of assault or attempted robbery—not both (Choice A).

📌 Educational Objective

Robbery requires a taking of the victim's property by force or intimidation. Since assault satisfies that intimidation requirement, it is a lesser included offense that merges with the completed robbery or attempted robbery.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子等到所有顾客都离开后，在一家小杂货店即将打烊时进入店内。他走到店里唯一的店员面前说：“把收银机里所有的钱都交出来，否则你会受伤。”店员晕倒，头部撞到了柜台边缘。当该男子走到柜台后面准备打开收银机时，两名顾客进入了店内。在该男子能够打开收银机抽屉之前，他跑了出去。

根据这些证据，该男子可以被恰当地定何种罪名？

zh-choices.A: 攻击罪和抢劫未遂罪。
zh-choices.B: 攻击罪和抢劫罪。
zh-choices.C: 抢劫未遂罪。
zh-choices.D: 抢劫罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：先威胁后没拿到钱，这种情况通常是未遂抢劫（attempted robbery），而不是既成抢劫（robbery）；袭击（assault）在这里只是抢劫的较轻包含罪，会合并掉。

三秒认题路径：

威胁取钱 → 还没得手 → 看抢劫要件 → 只能未遂 → 选 C

核心法律规则

抢劫（robbery）考场意思：必须同时有“拿走财物 + 用暴力或胁迫从被害人身上或在其控制范围内拿走 + قصد永久占有”的完整组合。

未遂抢劫（attempted robbery）考场意思：只要被告已经有偷抢的具体故意，并且做了推进犯罪的一步，就算最后没拿到钱，也还能定未遂。

袭击（assault）考场意思：本题里“不给就会受伤”的威胁已经够成胁迫，但它只是抢劫中“用武力或恐吓”的那一层，不能单独把“没拿到钱”补成既成抢劫。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用本题；本题真正锁定的是抢劫要件没完成，所以落在未遂，而不是既成抢劫。

思维导图

先看：有没有完成 robbery？
要件1有无“拿走并带走”财物？
没有：人跑了，收银抽屉还没打开。
要件2有无 force or intimidation？
有：他说“不给钱就会受伤”，这一步满足胁迫。
要件3有无永久占有故意？
有：他是来抢现金的，不是临时借用。
结论：完整 robbery 缺了“拿到钱”这一步。
下一问能否定 attempt？
能：有具体抢劫故意 + 威胁店员，已经是明显的实行行为。
所以：可定 attempted robbery，不是 robbery；assault 作为较轻包含罪并入，不单独再算一份。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他已经威胁、店员还晕倒了，好像“抢劫既遂”已经成立。

但考试真正问的是：钱有没有被拿走。司法考试看的是「法律结果有没有完成」，而不是「场面看起来够不够凶」。

这里最容易混的是 assault：它确实出现了，但它只是抢劫的胁迫工具，不能把“没完成取财”自动补成既遂。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 还没打开收银抽屉就跑了，说明 robbery 少了“取走财物”这一步，但他已用威胁推进抢钱，所以是 attempted robbery。

❌ 概念混淆 | 合并关系误判

✕ A: 把 assault 和未遂抢劫拆开算，忘了它会并入抢劫。

❌ 事实误判 | 既遂完成偷换

✕ B: 以为威胁一出口就算抢到钱了，题干其实没有完成取财。

❌ 法律适用 | 结果要件误套

✕ D: 只看到抢劫意图，忽略 carrying away 这一步没发生。

这题建议用什么方法？

先盯取财是否完成，再看威胁是否只是把案件推到未遂层级。

考场速记

记住：robbery 要“拿到东西”，attempted robbery 只要“朝着抢去做了动作”就够了；assault 在这里通常只是并入的较轻包含罪。

口诀：先看有没有“得手”，没得手但已威胁推进，就优先想未遂抢劫。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Upon the recent passing of her mother, a sister inherited a valuable antique chair that her brother had coveted for a long time. Unbeknownst to the sister, the brother had accumulated a large amount of gambling debt that required immediate payment, so he decided to steal the chair when he knew that his sister would be out with friends. Early the next evening, just after the sister left, the brother entered her home through the front door, which he knew she always left unlocked. After entering the living room, the brother grabbed the chair and quickly exited the home. The sister's neighbor, who happened to be outside getting her mail, noticed the brother as he was leaving. She was able to see his face because it was illuminated by the setting sun. Upon recognizing him, she immediately called the police and reported the crime she had just witnessed. The brother was subsequently arrested and charged with burglary.
In a common-law jurisdiction, is the brother guilty of burglary?

choices.A: No, because the front door to the sister's house was unlocked.
choices.B: No, because there was sufficient sunlight to see the brother's face.
choices.C: Yes, because the brother had the specific intent to commit robbery.
choices.D: Yes, because the brother intended to permanently deprive the sister of the chair.

questions.explanation:
Burglary

(common law v. modern (majority) definition)
Unlawful breaking and entry of another’s dwelling at night building/structure∨
with the specific intent to commit a felony ∧crime therein.

Common-law burglary is defined as the unlawful breaking and entering of another's dwelling at night with the specific intent to commit a felony therein—eg, larceny (as seen here). Nighttime is the period of darkness between sunset and sunrise. Therefore, it is not considered nighttime when there is sufficient natural daylight to see the burglar's face.

Here, the brother entered the sister's home early in the evening while she was out with friends, with the intent to steal the sister's chair. But since it was early in the evening, there was sufficient sunlight for the neighbor to see the brother's face when he was outside. Therefore, the common-law nighttime requirement for burglary was not met.

(Choice A) An unlawful breaking occurs when the defendant uses any degree of force to gain entry (eg, opening a door) without the owner's permission or legal privilege. Since the brother waited until his sister left the house before opening the door and entering the living room, this element is met even though the door was left unlocked.

(Choice C) Robbery is larceny committed in the victim's presence by force or intimidation. Here, the brother stole the sister's chair while she was out with friends—not in her presence.

(Choice D) Larceny is the unlawful taking and carrying away of another's personal property with the specific intent to permanently deprive the owner of that property (here, the chair). The brother entered the sister's home with the intent to commit this felony therein. But since the nighttime requirement has not also been met, he is not guilty of common-law burglary.

📌 Educational Objective

Common-law burglary is defined as the unlawful breaking and entering of another's dwelling at night with the specific intent to commit a felony therein. When there is sufficient natural daylight to see the burglar's face, it is not considered nighttime.

一名女子的母亲最近去世，她继承了一把价值不菲的古董椅，这把椅子是她哥哥垂涎已久的。妹妹不知道的是，哥哥累积了大量需要立即偿还的赌债，因此他决定在妹妹与朋友外出时偷走这把椅子。第二天傍晚，妹妹刚一离开，哥哥就通过他知道妹妹总是不锁的前门进入了她的家。进入客厅后，哥哥抓起椅子迅速离开了住宅。妹妹的邻居当时正好在外面取邮件，她注意到了正要离开的哥哥。由于夕阳的照射，她能看清他的脸。认出他后，她立即报警，报告了她刚刚目睹的犯罪行为。哥哥随后被逮捕，并被控以入室犯法罪 (burglary)。

在一个普通法 (common-law) 司法管辖区，该哥哥是否犯有入室犯法罪 (burglary)？

zh-choices.A: 不构成，因为妹妹家的前门没有上锁。
zh-choices.B: 不构成，因为当时有充足的日光，足以看清哥哥的脸。
zh-choices.C: 构成，因为哥哥有实施抢劫罪 (robbery) 的特定意图。
zh-choices.D: 构成，因为哥哥意图永久剥夺妹妹对椅子的所有权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：普通法 burglary 的关键门槛是“夜间”，不是门锁有没有锁，也不是偷了什么。

三秒认题路径：

破门入室 → 看是否夜间 → 能看清脸 → 不是夜间 → 无 burglary

核心法律规则

普通法入室盗窃（common-law burglary）要求：非法破门进入（breaking and entering）他人住宅（dwelling），并且发生在夜间（at night），还要带着进入后实施重罪（felony）的特定意图。这里的“夜间”不是抽象黄昏，而是sufficient natural daylight 还不能看清脸的黑暗时段；只要还能看清嫌疑人的脸，就通常不算夜间。

所以这题虽然有破门进入和偷椅子的意图，但决定输赢的只有一个点：邻居还能看清他的脸，说明夜间要件没过，burglary 直接卡死。

核心判例：本题按普通法定义处理，不需要额外判例展开；考点就是“能看清脸”会把“夜间”要件打掉。

思维导图

先看：是否是普通法 burglary？
门槛 1：非法 breaking and entering？
这里已满足：开门进屋也算 breaking
门槛 2：进入的是 dwelling？
这里已满足：妹妹的家就是 dwelling
门槛 3：是否 at night？
邻居还能看清脸 → 说明不是夜间
门槛 4：是否带着偷窃/重罪意图？
是，想拿椅子，意图这一步不救他。
结论：少了夜间要件 → 不是 burglary → 选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他是趁家里没人、又是从前门进去，听起来很像 burglary。

但考试真正问的是：at night 这个门槛有没有过；门锁开没开只是 breaking，不是决定胜负的点。

司法考试看的是「法律构成上能不能成立」，而不是「现场看起来多像小偷」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 能看清他的脸 说明还有足够自然光，普通法 burglary 的夜间要件没过，所以不能定罪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 门未上锁误判

✕ A: 把 unlocked 当成抗辩，忽略了开门也算 breaking。

❌ 事实误判 | 抢劫偷换

✕ C: 把偷椅子硬说成 robbery，题干根本没有当面暴力或胁迫。

❌ 法律适用 | 只看意图

✕ D: 只盯着 permanently deprive，忘了 burglary 还要夜间。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓普通法 burglary 四要件，再用“能不能看清脸”快速卡掉夜间。

考场速记

记住一句：burglary 先看“进屋”，再看“夜间”，最后看“偷什么”；只要还能看清脸，夜间通常就没了。

highlights.text: early the next evening

reason.en: This timing is central to whether the nighttime element is satisfied.
reason.zh: 该时点决定夜间要件是否成立。

highlights.text: just after the sister left

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A woman decided to steal a necklace that belonged to her neighbor. She knew where the neighbor kept the necklace because she had been in the neighbor's house on many occasions when the neighbor had taken off the necklace and put it away in a jewelry box in the bathroom. One night, the woman went to the neighbor's house. The neighbor was away, and the house was dark. The woman opened the bathroom window, saw the jewelry box on the counter, and started to climb inside. As her leg cleared the window sill, the neighbor's dog began to bark loudly. Terrified, the woman jumped back outside and fled.
The crimes below are listed in descending order of seriousness.
What is the most serious crime, if any, committed by the woman?

choices.A: Burglary.
choices.B: Attempted burglary.
choices.C: Attempted larceny.
choices.D: No crime.

questions.explanation:
In most jurisdictions, burglary is defined as the:

  • unlawful entry of a building or other structure
  • with the specific intent to commit any crime therein—even if that crime is not completed.

An unlawful entry occurs when any part of the defendant's body (or an object under his/her control) crosses into the structure without the possessor's consent or legal privilege. And the crime that burglars often intend to commit inside is larceny—ie, the unlawful taking and carrying away of another's personal property with the specific intent to permanently deprive that person of the property.

Here, the woman unlawfully entered her neighbor's house when her leg cleared the bathroom window sill. She did so with the specific intent to steal the neighbor's necklace. And although the woman did not succeed, she still committed burglary—the most serious of the listed crimes (Choices B & D). She also committed attempted larceny (the least serious crime) since she:

  • had the specific intent to commit larceny (ie, steal the necklace)
  • committed an act in furtherance of the larceny (ie, opened and entered the window)
  • but did not complete the crime (ie, failed to take the necklace) (Choice C).
📌 Educational Objective

Burglary is the unlawful entry of a building or other structure with the specific intent to commit a crime therein—but that crime need not be completed. An unlawful entry occurs when the defendant's body or an object under his/her control crosses into the structure without the possessor's permission or legal privilege.
questions.zh-question:
一名女子决定偷窃属于她邻居的一条项链。她知道邻居把项链放在哪里，因为她曾多次到邻居家，看到邻居摘下项链，并将其放入浴室的首饰盒里。一天晚上，该女子去了邻居家。邻居不在家，房子里一片漆黑。该女子打开浴室窗户，看到柜台上的首饰盒，然后开始往里爬。当她的腿越过窗台时，邻居的狗开始大声吠叫。该女子吓坏了，跳回外面逃走了。

以下罪行按严重程度降序排列。

该女子所犯下的最严重的罪行是什么（如果有的话）？

zh-choices.A: 入室犯法罪 (Burglary)。
zh-choices.B: 入室犯法罪未遂。
zh-choices.C: 盗窃罪未遂。
zh-choices.D: 无罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：入室盗窃（burglary）只看“非法进入 + 进入时就有意图犯罪”，不要求把东西真的偷走。

三秒认题路径：

开窗进屋 → 进门瞬间 → 已想偷项链 → 侵入成立 → 选 burglary

核心法律规则

入室盗窃（burglary）在多数州要求：未经许可进入建筑物或其他结构，并且在进入时就带着在屋内实施犯罪的特定意图。

非法进入（unlawful entry）的考场意思：身体任何一部分，或自己控制下的物体，只要跨进结构内部，就算进入了。

这里还不需要把目标犯罪做完；只要进入时就打算偷，就够构成 burglary。盗窃（larceny）则是把别人的财物拿走并打算永久据为己有。

核心判例：无特定单独判例也能稳答；本题按普通法 burglary 规则判断：进入时有偷窃意图即可，不等于必须完成盗窃。

思维导图

先看：有没有 非法进入（unlawful entry）？
有女人打开浴室窗户，腿越过窗台，身体进入住宅内部。
再看：进入时有没有 特定意图（specific intent）？
有她一开始就是冲着项链去的，目标是屋内实施 larceny。
最后卡点：目标犯罪有没有做完？
不需要完成偷窃；第三要件失败也不救她，burglary 已成立。
结论最严重罪名是 burglary，不是 attempted burglary。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她最后什么都没偷到，所以最多只是 attempted larceny。

但考试真正问的是：她在进入房屋那一刻已经带着偷项链的意图，burglary 的门槛已经过了。

司法考试看的是「进入时有没有犯罪意图」，不是「最后有没有把赃物拿到手」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 leg cleared the bathroom window sill 说明她已进入住宅，且进屋时就想偷项链，所以 burglary 已完成。

❌ 法律适用 | 完成要件误判

✕ B: 把 completed 当成必需，但 burglary 不等盗窃成功。

❌ 概念混淆 | 罪名层级误判

✕ C: 只看到没拿走项链，忘了先前的非法进入已把 burglary 做实。

❌ 事实误判 | 侵入事实漏读

✕ D: 忽略了 leg cleared，她其实已经跨进屋内。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓进入是否发生，再抓进入时的主观意图，最后别被“没偷成”带偏。

考场速记

记忆口诀：进入时有意图，没偷成也算 burglary。看到“unlawful entry + intent to commit a crime”就先锁定入室盗窃。

reason.zh: 表明在未经同意的情况下制造入口的物理行为。

reason.en: Indicates that a part of the body crossed the threshold, completing the entry.

reason.en: Explains why the target crime (larceny) was not completed, though burglary was already complete.

reason.en: Correct because both entry and specific intent elements were completed.
reason.zh: 正确，因为进入和特定意图要件均已完成。

reason.en: Incorrectly assumes that full body entry is required for a completed burglary.
reason.zh: 错误地认为既遂入室盗窃需要整个身体进入。

reason.en: While the woman did commit attempted larceny, burglary is a more serious completed crime.
reason.zh: 虽然该女子确实犯了盗窃未遂，但入室盗窃是更严重的既遂犯罪。

reason.en: Fails to recognize that liability attached once the window sill was crossed with felonious intent.
reason.zh: 未能认识到一旦怀有重罪意图跨越窗台，刑事责任即已成立。

highlights.text: decided to steal a necklace

reason.en: Establishes the required mental state (intent to commit a crime therein) for burglary.
reason.zh: 确立了入室盗窃所需的心理状态（在此处实施犯罪的意图）。

highlights.text: leg cleared the window sill

reason.en: The critical fact showing that the entry element of burglary was fully satisfied.
reason.zh: 表明入室盗窃的进入要件已完全满足的关键事实。

highlights.text: What is the most serious crime, if any, committed by the woman?

reason.en: Requires comparing multiple offenses to find the most serious completed or attempted crime.
reason.zh: 需要比较多项罪行以找出最严重的既遂或未遂犯罪。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
One evening on a college campus, a student handed a classmate cash and the classmate gave the student a packet of heroin. The student looked at the packet and went to place it in his pants pocket. An off-duty police officer who was taking classes at the college witnessed the transaction from only a few feet away. The officer immediately identified herself as a police officer and told the participants that they were under arrest. The student, who had been in the act of placing the packet in his pants pocket, dropped the packet and unsuccessfully attempted to flee.
The student was charged with possession of heroin. At trial, the student offered evidence, which the prosecution did not dispute, that the cash was not transferred in payment for the heroin but instead to repay a loan the classmate had made to the student.
Can the student properly be convicted?

choices.A: No, because the student did not pay for the heroin.
choices.B: No, because the student did not place the heroin in his pocket.
choices.C: Yes, because the student had the opportunity to cease dominion and control over the heroin.
choices.D: Yes, because the student handled the heroin packet.

Exercise of dominion and control

A defendant can be convicted of possession of a controlled substance (or other prohibited object) if the prosecution establishes that the defendant knowingly possessed the controlled substance. The possession element requires proof that the defendant either:

  • knowingly received an illegal substance or
  • exercised dominion and control over the substance after learning of its illegal character.

Here, the student may not have initially known that the classmate had given the student a packet of heroin. However, the student had time to look at the packet and went to place it in his pants pocket before the police officer intervened. This shows that the student exercised dominion and control over the heroin. As a result, the student can be properly convicted.

(Choice A) This crime does not require proof that the defendant acquired the substance by paying for it. Therefore, the fact that the student gave the classmate cash to repay a loan—not to pay for the heroin—is irrelevant.

(Choice B) The student did not need to secure the heroin in his pocket to be convicted of possessing it because the prosecution need only prove that the student exercised something more than fleeting or momentary control.

(Choice D) Mere handling of a controlled substance is not necessarily sufficient to establish possession. For example, a person who is unexpectedly given a packet containing a controlled substance may handle it to ascertain its contents and then immediately discard it. Under those circumstances, the element of possession is not met.

📌 Educational Objective

Possession offenses require proof that the defendant (1) knowingly received an illegal item or (2) exercised dominion and control over the item after learning of its illegal character.

📚 References
  • Wayne R. LaFave, 1 Substantive Criminal Law § 6.1(e) (3d ed. 2020)
questions.zh-question:
一天晚上，在大学校园里，一名学生递给同学一些现金，该同学则给了这名学生一包海洛因。该学生看了看那包东西，并准备将其放入自己的裤袋。一名正在该大学上课的休班警官在几英尺外目睹了这笔交易。该警官立即表明身份，并告知交易双方他们被逮捕了。那名学生正要将包裹放入口袋，他扔掉了包裹并试图逃跑，但没有成功。

该学生被控犯有持有海洛因罪。在审判中，该学生提供了证据，检察官对此没有异议，即现金的转移并非为了支付海洛因的费用，而是为了偿还该同学之前借给他的贷款。

该学生是否可以被合法定罪？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为该学生没有为海洛因付款。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为该学生没有将海洛因放入口袋。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为该学生曾有机会放弃对海洛因的支配和控制。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为该学生接触了那包海洛因。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：持有毒品（possession）看的是你有没有对毒品形成支配和控制（dominion and control），不是看你有没有把它揣稳或是不是付钱买的。

三秒认题路径：

拿到海洛因 → 看到内容 → 放入口袋 → 先于警察介入 → 已有支配控制

核心法律规则

持有型犯罪里，检方只要证明被告明知持有（knowingly possessed）即可。考场意思：你不一定要亲手买来，也不一定要一直攥在手里；只要你知道它是什么，而且对它有过超过一瞬间的支配和控制（dominion and control），就可能成立。

如果被告在知道是违禁物后，仍然把它拿着、查看、准备放入口袋，这通常就够了。考场意思：这里不是问“有没有完成交易”，而是问“有没有在警察介入前已经碰到足够久，形成占有”。

核心判例： LaFave 相关规则强调：持有可以来自“明知接收”或“知情后继续支配控制”，本题落在后者。

思维导图

先看：这不是“有没有买毒品”，而是“有没有形成持有”
第一步：学生先看了包装，再准备把它放进裤袋，说明不是纯路过碰一下。
第二步：警察亮明身份并宣布逮捕前，学生已经在处理这包海洛因，属于支配和控制。
第三步：被告没必要把毒品稳稳塞进口袋；“没放好”不等于“没持有”
结论：能定罪，因为关键不是付款，而是已经对毒品形成了可归责的持有状态。
答案：C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然这笔现金只是还借款，不是买毒品，那就不算持有。

但考试真正问的是：有没有对海洛因形成过知情后的支配和控制，而不是钱到底是不是毒资。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

另一个常见误区是以为必须把毒品牢牢放进口袋才算数；其实只要不是一闪而过的接触，短暂掌控也可能足够。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

学生已经看过海洛因并准备放入口袋，在警察介入前已对毒品形成支配和控制，所以可以定罪。

❌ 事实误判 | 付款偷换

✕ A: 把付款当成持有要件，paid for it 不是本题门槛。

❌ 法律适用 | 口袋误判

✕ B: 误以为必须真塞进口袋才算，短暂控制也能成立持有。

❌ 概念混淆 | 仅碰触混同

✕ D: 把handled 直接等同持有，忽略还要看是否知情后继续控制。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“知不知道是毒品”，再看“有没有在被打断前形成支配和控制”。

考场速记

记住一句：持有 = 明知接收，或者知道后继续控制；不是“必须买过”，也不是“必须稳稳收好”。

这类题先找知情 + 控制，再排除“付款”“装进口袋”这些会误导你的背景细节。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man intended to rob a local convenience store that was rumored to contain a large safe. One night, the man walked into the convenience store, pointed a gun at the store owner, and demanded to know where the safe was kept. Frightened, the store owner pointed to a storage room located at the back of the store and approximately 20 feet from where the man and the store owner were standing. The man then moved the store owner to the storage room and forced him to open the safe. The man fled after taking the money in the safe, and the store owner immediately called the police. The man was later arrested and charged with robbery and kidnapping.
Can the man be properly convicted of kidnapping?

choices.A: No, because the man did not move the store owner more than was necessary to complete the robbery.
choices.B: No, because the storage room was only 20 feet away from the store owner.
choices.C: Yes, because the man unlawfully moved the store owner into the storage room during the commission of the robbery.
choices.D: Yes, because the man's conduct amounted to confinement of the store owner.

questions.explanation:
Kidnapping
Common law Forcibly abducting or stealing person from his/her own country & sending to another country
MPC Unlawfully moving or confining another to:
  • hold for ransom or as hostage
  • facilitate commission of felony or flight thereafter
  • injure/terrorize victim or another or
  • interfere with governmental/political function
Modern view General Intentional & unlawful confinement involving:
  • some movement (asportation) or
  • concealment
Aggravated General kidnapping committed for:
  • ransom
  • commission of other crime
  • offensive purpose or
  • child stealing
MPC = Model Penal Code.

Kidnapping is:

  • the intentional and unlawful confinement of another
  • against that person's will (eg, by force, threat, or fraud)
  • coupled with either moving or hiding that person.

A perpetrator need only move the victim a short distance—even a few feet—to satisfy the movement (ie, asportation) element of kidnapping (Choice B). However, for a kidnapping to occur incident to the commission of another offense, the movement of the victim must be more than is necessary to complete the other offense.* Otherwise, the perpetrator cannot be convicted of kidnapping.

Here, the man entered the store intending to commit robbery. The man then pointed a gun at the store owner (force) and moved him into the storage room (confinement) so that the store owner could open the safe. But since the movement of the store owner was no more than was necessary to complete the robbery, the man cannot be properly convicted of kidnapping (Choices C & D).

*Courts will consider several factors, including (1) the duration and significance of the movement, (2) whether the movement was an inherent part or independent of the other offense, and (3) whether the movement made the other offense easier to commit.

📌 Educational Objective

For a kidnapping to occur incident to the commission of another offense, the victim must be moved more than is necessary to complete the other offense.
questions.zh-question: 一名男子打算抢劫（rob）一家当地便利店，据传该店有一个大保险箱。一天晚上，该男子走进便利店，用枪指着店主，并要求知道保险箱放在哪里。店主受惊后，指向商店后面一个储藏室，该储藏室距离男子和店主站立的位置大约20英尺。该男子随后将店主带到储藏室，并强迫他打开保险箱。男子拿走保险箱里的钱后逃跑，店主立即报警。该男子后来被捕，并被控抢劫（robbery）和绑架（kidnapping）。该男子能否被恰当地定罪绑架（kidnapping）？

zh-choices.A: 不能，因为该男子移动店主的距离并未超出完成抢劫（robbery）所必需的范围。
zh-choices.B: 不能，因为储藏室距离店主只有20英尺。
zh-choices.C: 能，因为该男子在实施抢劫（robbery）过程中非法将店主带入储藏室。
zh-choices.D: 能，因为该男子的行为构成了对店主的禁闭（confinement）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes Against the Person

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：绑架（kidnapping）在抢劫过程中成立的门槛，是不是把被害人的移动做得超过完成抢劫所必需的程度。

三秒认题路径：

抢劫中挪人 → 先想绑架 → 看移动幅度 → 是否超必要 → 不能成立

核心法律规则

这题只要抓住这一条

绑架（kidnapping）考场意思：把人非法带走或关住，而且是违背其意愿，还要伴随一定的移动或藏匿。

但如果绑架只是附带在另一项犯罪里，考试重点就变成：被害人的移动必须多于完成原罪所必需。如果只是为了把抢劫做完，那通常不能再单独算绑架。

所以这题不是问“有没有移动”，而是问“这个移动是不是超量”。

核心判例：本题不需要特定判例名；考点锁定在“抢劫附带的移动是否超过完成抢劫所必需”的现代绑架规则。

思维导图

先问：这是不是终局后才能救济的那种“小移动”争议？
事实触发：持枪抢劫时，把店主从柜台边挪到后方储物间。
法律关卡：绑架（kidnapping）要看移动是否超过完成抢劫所需。
卡死点：只为打开保险箱而移动，属于完成抢劫的一部分，不够“超量”
结论：不能仅凭这次移动就把抢劫再加成绑架。
答题口令：看到“抢劫中顺手挪人” → 先查“是否多于必要” → 否则选无绑架。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：只要把人从一个地方挪到另一个地方，就已经有绑架了。

但考试真正问的是：这个移动是不是只是为了把抢劫做完；如果只是让店主走到储物间开保险箱，那它仍然是抢劫的配套动作。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干把店主移到储物间只是为了打开保险箱，这次移动没有超过完成抢劫所必需的程度，所以不能再按绑架定罪。

❌ 事实误判 | 距离误读

✕ B: 只盯着20 feet，忘了关键是是否超出抢劫所需。

❌ 法律适用 | 移动即绑架

✕ C: 把“有移动”直接等同绑架，漏掉了超必要这道门槛。

❌ 概念混淆 | 关押偷换

✕ D: 把抢劫时的配套控制当成独立confinement，其实只是完成抢劫的手段。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否是“抢劫附带移动”，再问这一步有没有超出完成抢劫的必要范围。

考场速记

记住一句话：绑架不是“挪了人就算”，而是“挪人的幅度要超过完成原罪所需”。

本题速记：抢劫中顺手挪人，先问“有没有超量”；没超量，就别把它升级成绑架。

keywords.text: forced him to open the safe

reason.zh: 表明该移动是为了完成抢劫。

reason.en: Frames the issue as whether kidnapping is separately sustainable.
reason.zh: 提示争点是绑架能否作为独立罪名成立。

A.text: more than was necessary to complete the robbery

reason.en: States the correct limiting rule for kidnapping during another offense.

reason.zh: 只强调移动本身，忽略了附随抢劫的限制。

D.text: amounted to confinement of the store owner

reason.en: Suggests confinement alone is enough, ignoring the robbery-incident rule.
reason.zh: 暗示仅有拘禁即可成立，忽略了附随抢劫规则。

highlights.text: moved the store owner to the storage room

reason.en: This is the act alleged to constitute kidnapping.
reason.zh: 这是被指称构成绑架的行为。

highlights.text: approximately 20 feet from where the man and the store owner were standing

reason.en: The short distance tempts a wrong focus on asportation alone.
reason.zh: 短距离容易让人误以为仅看移动距离即可。

highlights.text: during the commission of the robbery

reason.en: This signals the special rule limiting kidnapping when another crime is being committed.
reason.zh: 提示在实施其他犯罪时绑架适用特殊限制规则。

highlights.text: forced him to open the safe

reason.en: Shows the movement was used to facilitate the robbery.
reason.zh: 表明该移动是为了帮助完成抢劫。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A driver stopped at a red traffic light in his home state. A stranger opened the passenger door, got in, and pointed a gun at the driver. The stranger then directed the driver to keep driving. They drove several miles, crossed into a neighboring state, and drove several more miles.
When they reached a remote location, the stranger ordered the driver to pull over. The stranger then robbed the driver of his wallet and cash and ordered him out of the car. The stranger drove off in the driver's car.
The stranger is charged with kidnapping in the neighboring state, which has adopted the Model Penal Code.
Can the stranger properly be convicted of kidnapping in the neighboring state?

choices.A: No, because any kidnapping took place in the driver's home state.
choices.B: No, because the restraint was incidental to the robbery.
choices.C: Yes, because the driver in effect paid a ransom for his release.
choices.D: Yes, because the driver was transported under threat of force in the neighboring state.

questions.explanation:
Kidnapping under Model Penal Code

Victim intentionally & unlawfully:
or
Moved
  • from home/business or
  • substantial distance from
    place found
Confined
  • for substantial period and
  • in isolated place
Purpose
  • ransom/reward or hostage/shield
  • aid commission of, or flight from, felony
  • inflict bodily injury/terrorize victim or another
  • interfere with governmental function
More than incidental to other crime
  • long distance or duration
  • increased danger

A defendant can be prosecuted in any state where an essential part of the crime has occurred without violating double jeopardy. Under the Model Penal Code, kidnapping occurs when a victim is intentionally and unlawfully moved (or confined) for any of the following purposes:

  • to hold for ransom/reward or as a hostage/shield
  • to facilitate commission of any felony or flight thereafter
  • to inflict bodily injury on or terrorize the victim or another
  • to interfere with performance of a governmental or political function

An unlawful movement occurs when the victim is (1) removed from his/her residence or business or (2) taken a substantial distance from where he/she is found. And the movement must be more than incidental to the commission of another crime. To make this determination, courts consider the distance and duration of the movement as well as the increased danger the movement posed to the victim.

Here, the stranger entered the car, pointed a gun at the driver, and unlawfully forced him to drive a substantial distance into a neighboring state. This was done so that the stranger could rob the driver of his wallet, cash, and car. And since the driver was (1) forced to drive several miles in the neighboring state and (2) at risk of being shot while doing so, his kidnapping was more than incidental to the robbery (Choice B). As a result, the stranger can be convicted of kidnapping in the neighboring state.

(Choice A) The kidnapping did not only occur in the driver's home state because he was forced to drive across state lines.

(Choice C) A defendant can be convicted of kidnapping for moving a victim to hold for ransom. But the driver did not pay a ransom since the stolen cash, wallet, and car were not given in exchange for his release.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the Model Penal Code, unlawfully moving a victim a substantial distance through two states to facilitate a crime constitutes kidnapping in both states.

📚 References
  • Model Penal Code § 212.1 (Am. Law Inst. 2019) (kidnapping).
questions.zh-question:
一名司机在他居住的州（本州）等红灯时停下了车。一名陌生人打开副驾驶座的车门，进入车内，并用枪指着司机。然后，这名陌生人指示司机继续开车。他们行驶了数英里，进入了邻近的一个州，并又行驶了数英里。

当他们到达一个偏僻地点时，陌生人命令司机靠边停车。随后，陌生人抢走了司机的钱包和现金，并命令他下车。陌生人开着司机的车扬长而去。

这名陌生人在邻州被指控犯有绑架罪，该州已采纳《模范刑法典》(Model Penal Code)。

这名陌生人是否可以在邻州被恰当地定为绑架罪？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为任何绑架行为都发生在司机的本州。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为该限制行为是抢劫罪的附带行为。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为司机实际上为自己的获释支付了赎金。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为司机在邻州是在武力威胁下被转移的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes Against the Person

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：Model Penal Code 下，跨州被强迫驾车移动是否构成 kidnapping（绑架），以及能不能在邻州起诉定罪。

三秒认题路径：

强迫开车 → 跨州移动 → 为了抢劫 → 非附带 → 能定绑架

核心法律规则

抓住这条规则就够了

绑架（kidnapping） 在 Model Penal Code（模范刑法典） 下，不只是“把人弄走”，而是要把受害人故意且非法地移动（unlawfully moved），并且目的属于法定类型之一。对这题最关键的是：为了促进其他重罪（facilitate commission of any felony）而移动，而且移动必须超过附带程度（more than incidental）。

这里的“超过附带程度”考场意思是：不是顺手挪一下就算，而是移动距离、持续时间、危险性都要够重。只要受害人被强迫开了几英里、还跨州，而且一路都被枪威胁，考试通常就会判定成绑架，不会被“这只是抢劫顺带发生的控制”带偏。

核心判例： Model Penal Code § 212.1 - 跨州强迫移动受害人以便利抢劫，属于绑架；关键是移动本身超过了抢劫的附带控制。

思维导图

先看：受害人是不是被故意且非法地移动了？
是 被枪指着从红灯处一路强迫开车，后来还跨过州界。
再看：移动的目的是不是为了促进抢劫（facilitate a felony）？
是 先逼车，再抢钱包、现金和车，目的很明显是便利抢劫。
最后卡死：这个移动只是抢劫的附带控制吗？
不是。几英里 + 跨州 + 枪口威胁 = more than incidental
结论：邻州能不能定绑架？
能 因为邻州里也发生了重要的非法移动，所以选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这只是抢劫时顺便控制司机，所以应该算“附带动作”。

但考试真正问的是：移动有没有超过抢劫所必需的最低控制，而这里已经是被逼着开很远、还跨州了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干显示受害人被枪逼着在邻州继续开了几英里，属于 跨州的非法移动，而且是为了抢劫，已超过附带程度，所以能在邻州定绑架。

❌ 事实误判 | 州界遗漏

✕ A: 把移动地点只算在出发州，漏掉了邻州里的关键行为。

❌ 概念混淆 | 附带误读

✕ B: 以为 incidental 只要沾上抢劫就没事，但这里移动太远、太危险了。

❌ 法律适用 | 赎金套错

✕ C: 把“赎金”硬套进来，但司机根本没有为获释交出任何对价。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓 MPC kidnapping 的“移动 + 目的 + 超过附带程度”，再问邻州里有没有完成关键行为。

考场速记

记住一句：“跨州强迫移动 + 为了重罪 + 不只是顺手控制”，通常就是绑架。

记忆口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 主要是给中间上诉例外用的；本题不是上诉题，但你要知道 kidnapping（绑架） 看的是“移动是否超过附带程度”，不是“抢劫里有没有顺便带走人”。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man loaned $200 to a friend, and the friend promised to repay the loan within a week. The friend's brother was present when the loan was made but otherwise was not involved in the loan arrangement. Two weeks later, the man encountered the friend's brother on the street. Because the man honestly, but unreasonably, believed that the friend's brother had promised to repay the loan if the friend did not, the man confronted the friend's brother and demanded immediate repayment of the loan. When the friend's brother refused, the man pulled out a gun and repeated his demand. The friend's brother took $200 from his wallet and handed it to the man.
Is the man guilty of robbery?

choices.A: No, because the man honestly believed that the friend's brother had promised to repay the loan.
choices.B: No, because the man was collecting a debt owed to him under a claim of right.
choices.C: Yes, because the man enforced his demand for repayment of the loan with a gun.
choices.D: Yes, because the man's belief that the friend's brother promised to repay the loan was unreasonable.

questions.explanation:
Robbery

Larceny
by either
Threat of force
Use of force

Larceny is the unlawful taking and carrying away of the victim's property with the intent to permanently deprive the victim of that property (i.e., intent to steal). But the defendant can be convicted of the more serious crime of robbery if:

  • the property was taken from the victim's person or presence and
  • the taking was achieved by force or intimidation.

The requisite intent for larceny does not exist when the defendant intends to take money as repayment of a debt. However, a majority of jurisdictions do not recognize this claim of right as a justification for robbery due to public policy, as robbery encompasses the use of force and threats to collect such debts.

Here, the man loaned $200 to a friend. The man honestly but unreasonably believed that the friend's brother promised to repay the loan if the friend did not. The man later demanded $200 from the brother and eventually took the $200 by force. But even though the man took the money as repayment of a debt, he committed robbery—not larceny—because he enforced his demand for repayment of the loan with a gun. Because this constitutes robbery, a claim-of-right defense is unavailable (Choice C). Therefore, the man is guilty of robbery.

(Choice A) The man did honestly believe that the friend's brother had promised to repay the loan. But this does not negate the requisite intent for robbery, as most jurisdictions do not recognize claim of right as a justification for robbery.

(Choice D) A defendant's claim of right—even if incorrect and unreasonable—is a defense to larceny (i.e., mistake of fact). But most jurisdictions do not recognize a claim-of-right defense to robbery (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

The requisite intent for larceny does not exist when the defendant intends to take money as repayment of a debt—i.e., claim of right. But based on public policy, most jurisdictions do not recognize claim of right as a justification for robbery.

一名男子借给一位朋友200美元，朋友承诺在一周内归还。借款时，朋友的兄弟也在场，但除此之外并未参与该借款安排。两周后，该男子在街上遇到了朋友的兄弟。由于该男子真诚但不合理地相信朋友的兄弟曾承诺：如果朋友不还款，他会代为偿还这笔贷款，于是该男子拦住朋友的兄弟并要求其立即偿还该笔贷款。朋友的兄弟拒绝后，该男子掏出手枪并再次提出要求。朋友的兄弟从钱包里拿出200美元并交给了该男子。
该男子是否构成 robbery（抢劫）？

zh-choices.A: 不构成，因为该男子真诚地相信朋友的兄弟曾承诺偿还该贷款。
zh-choices.B: 不构成，因为该男子是在根据 claim of right（权利主张）追讨一笔欠他的债务。
zh-choices.C: 构成，因为该男子以手枪强迫对方满足其贷款偿还要求。
zh-choices.D: 构成，因为该男子认为朋友的兄弟承诺偿还贷款的信念是不合理的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Robbery

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：抢劫（robbery）里，索债抗辩（claim of right）通常不能挡住你用枪去收钱。

三秒认题路径：

要回债 → 持枪逼迫 → 取走现金 → 不是护债 → 判抢劫

核心法律规则

抢劫（robbery）= 从被害人本人或在其在场范围内拿走财物，并且是靠暴力或恐吓（force or intimidation）完成。考场意思：你只要是“拿钱时带着威胁”，就会往抢劫方向走。

索债抗辩（claim of right）常能影响的是偷窃（larceny）的“想偷”要件；但大多数州不把它当成抢劫的正当化理由。考场意思：你以为自己在“讨债”，也不能用枪把私人账单升级成合法收款。

所以，这题只要看到“gun + 逼对方立刻给钱 + 钱是当场交出来的”，结论就已经偏向抢劫，不是单纯的债务催收。

核心判例： claim of right 通常只救不了抢劫；公共政策不允许用武力收债。

思维导图

先看：他是不是在“收债”?
是： 继续问，这笔“债”是怎么收的？
关键动作： 先口头催，再拔枪威胁（threat of force），最后拿到 $200。
规则关卡： claim of right 可能影响 larceny，但抢劫看的是“有没有暴力/恐吓去拿财物”。
卡死点：public policy 不让你用枪收债，所以这个借口不能把抢劫洗掉。
结论： 即使他真以为对方欠钱，也仍然是 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他是在要回自己认为应得的钱，应该有 claim of right。

但考试真正问的是：他是不是把“讨债”做成了“用枪逼钱”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这道题里，真正坏掉的是收钱方式，不是他主观上有没有“债”的影子。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的 pulled out a gun 直接把“索债”变成了靠恐吓取财；抢劫只看暴力或恐吓完成取财，所以成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把真诚误信当成抢劫挡箭牌，但这只是在碰 honestly believed 的幻觉。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间抗辩误判

✕ B: 你抓住“讨债”就想直接免罪，但 claim of right 不是抢劫的通行证。

❌ 事实误判 | 题干条件偷换

✕ D: 误信不合理只会让你多想一步，但这题的败点在 with a gun，不是信念是否合理。

这题建议用什么方法？

先盯取财方式，再看抗辩能否覆盖暴力收债；这里先天被枪支威胁卡死。

考场速记

记住一句：claim of right 能救的多是 larceny，不是 robbery；一旦你靠force or intimidation收钱，通常就别再想拿“我只是讨债”当挡箭牌。

速记：“想要的是债，做出来的是抢。”

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A woman broke off her engagement to a man but refused to return the engagement ring the man had given her. One night, the man entered the woman's house after midnight to retrieve the ring. Although the woman was not at home, a neighbor saw the man enter the house and called the police. The man unsuccessfully searched for the ring for 10 minutes. As he was walking out the front door, the police arrived and immediately arrested him.
The man has been charged with burglary in a jurisdiction that follows the common law.
Which of the following, if proved, would serve as the man's best defense to the charge?

choices.A: The man incorrectly and unreasonably believed that he was legally entitled to the ring.
choices.B: The man knew that no one was at home when he entered the house.
choices.C: The man knew that the woman kept a key under the doormat and he used the key to enter the house.
choices.D: The man took nothing of value from the house.

questions.explanation:
Applicability of mistake-of-fact defense
Type of mens rea
Strict liability crime (eg, statutory rape)
Never a defense
Specific intent (eg, first-degree murder)
Honest mistake
negates specific
intent
General intent & malice (eg, involuntary manslaughter)
Honest & reasonable
mistake negates
mens rea

Common law burglary is the unlawful breaking and entering of another's dwelling at night with the specific intent to commit a felony therein. The intended felony is often larceny—ie:

  • the unlawful taking and carrying away of another's personal property
  • with the specific intent to permanently deprive the owner of that property.

Therefore, a defendant's belief that he/she is entitled to the property—even if incorrect and unreasonable—serves as a defense to larceny since it negates the intent requirement (ie, mistake of fact defense). And if larceny is the intended felony for common law burglary, that belief is also a defense to burglary.

Here, the man unlawfully entered the woman's house after midnight to retrieve the engagement ring he had given her. But he did not intend to commit a felony (ie, larceny) therein because he believed that he was legally entitled to that ring. Although this belief was incorrect and unreasonable, it still negates the intent requirement for larceny—and therefore burglary. As a result, this belief is the man's best defense.

(Choice B) Common law burglary has no requirement that the dwelling be occupied at the time of entry. Therefore, it is no defense that the man knew that no one was at the woman's home when he entered.

(Choice C) Since a "breaking" occurs when any amount of force is used to enter a dwelling (eg, pushing an already-open door), the man's use of a key to enter the home would satisfy this requirement—not negate it.

(Choice D) Common law burglary requires an intent to commit a felony inside another's dwelling, but that felony need not be completed. Therefore, the fact that the man took nothing of value from the house (ie, did not commit larceny) is no defense to burglary.

📌 Educational Objective

Larceny requires the intent to permanently deprive another of his/her property, so a person who takes property under the belief that he/she owns it is not guilty of this crime. And if larceny serves as the intended felony for common law burglary, this belief would be a defense to both crimes.
questions.zh-question:
一名女子与一名男子解除了婚约，但拒绝归还该男子送给她的订婚戒指。一天晚上，该男子在午夜后进入该女子家中，试图取回戒指。尽管该女子当时不在家，但一位邻居看到该男子进入房屋并报了警。该男子花了10分钟寻找戒指，但未成功。就在他走出前门时，警察赶到并立即逮捕了他。

在一个遵循普通法的司法管辖区，该男子被指控犯有入室犯法罪（burglary）。

以下哪一项如果得到证实，将构成该男子对此项指控的最佳辩护？

zh-choices.A: 该男子不正确且不合理地相信，他在法律上有权获得该戒指。
zh-choices.B: 该男子进入房屋时知道家中无人。
zh-choices.C: 该男子知道该女子在门垫下藏有钥匙，并用该钥匙进入房屋。
zh-choices.D: 该男子没有从房屋中取走任何有价值的物品。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：普通法 burglary 里，若被告以为自己有权拿走屋内财物，这种错误信念能不能否定其“入室时意图实施 felony”的要件。

三秒认题路径：

common law burglary → 进屋时意图 → 目标是 larceny → 误以为有权 → 可作最佳抗辩

核心法律规则

普通法 入室盗窃（burglary） 要求：夜间 非法破门进入（breaking and entering） 他人住宅，并且在进入时具有实施 重罪（felony） 的特定意图。

这里常见的目标重罪是 盗窃（larceny）；而 larceny 需要“拿走他人财物 + قصد 永久剥夺”这一意图，所以如果被告真诚地以为自己有权拿这件东西，就会把这个意图打掉。

这个题里，mistake of fact 不是在帮他“洗白结果”，而是在帮他否定进入时的主观要件；所以只要 larceny 的意图没成立，burglary 也就跟着断掉。

核心判例： 题目没有要求死背特定案件名；考场只要抓住“对财物权属的错误信念可否定 larceny 意图”，就能锁定 burglary 结论。

思维导图

先看：被告进入住宅时，心里到底想做什么？
YES 分支
相信自己有权拿回 engagement ring
误以为不是“偷”
这份信念是否影响 burglary 的核心意图？
是
杀点：larceny 需要永久剥夺意图；真诚误信有权 → 意图没成立
结论：可作最佳抗辩 → 不成立 common law burglary
NO 分支
B：知道没人在家 → 没用
occupancy 不是普通法要件
C：用 doormat 下的 key 进门 → 仍算 breaking
不是抗辩点
D：没拿走值钱东西 → 不影响
未完成 larceny 也可成立 burglary

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他是来拿回自己的戒指，而且最后也没偷到东西，所以好像不该算 burglary。

但考试真正问的是：他在进门那一刻有没有 意图实施盗窃（intent to commit larceny）。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

真正能救他的，不是“结果没成功”，而是“他对财物权属的错误信念直接打掉了 larceny 的主观要件”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干关键是他 误以为自己有权拿回戒指，这会否定 larceny 需要的永久剥夺意图；既然 intended felony 站不住，burglary 也一起倒下。

❌ 事实误判 | 住户在家误读

✕ B: 把 no one was at home 当成关键，但普通法 burglary 不要求屋内有人。

❌ 法律适用 | 破门概念误判

❌ 概念混淆 | 未遂完成混为一谈

✕ D: 看到没拿走值钱东西就想放人，但 burglary 看的是进入时的意图，不看 larceny 最后成没成。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定 burglary 的“进入时意图”，再回头问这个意图有没有被 mistake of fact 打掉。

考场速记

记住这句：对自己财物的真诚误信 可以打掉 larceny 意图；而 burglary 如果把 larceny 当作 intended felony，也会一起被打掉。

速记：“先看进门时想什么，再看这个想法有没有把 felony 意图掐掉。”

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
An unemployed man was planning to rob a convenience store and staked out the store for several weeks. One evening, the man opened and entered through the front door of the store just before closing time and reached for the gun in his waistband as he approached the checkout counter. However, upon seeing the elderly clerk who reminded the man of his grandfather, the man changed his mind and ran out of the store. Finding the man's behavior suspicious, the clerk called the police, who later apprehended the man and charged him with burglary.
In the jurisdiction, burglary is defined as "breaking and entering any building or structure with the intent to commit a felony or to steal therein."
Is the man likely to be found guilty of burglary?

choices.A: No, because the man had permission to enter the convenience store.
choices.B: No, because the man is guilty of only attempted burglary of the convenience store.
choices.C: Yes, because the man intentionally broke into and entered the convenience store.
choices.D: Yes, because the man lost his status as an invitee when he entered the convenience store with the intent to commit robbery.

questions.explanation:
This jurisdiction defines burglary as:

  • the breaking and entering of any building or structure
  • with the intent to commit a felony (eg, robbery) or to steal therein.

Breaking occurs when the defendant uses any degree of force to gain entry (eg, opening a door), and entering occurs when any part of the defendant's body or an object in his/her possession crosses into the structure. The breaking and entering also must have been unlawful—ie, without the owner's permission or legal privilege. A business gives the public permission to enter its premises during business hours, but not when it is closed.

Here, the man opened the front door and entered the convenience store with the intent to commit a robbery therein (Choice C). But since the store was still open to the public at that time, the man entered the store with the owner's permission. As a result, the man's entry was lawful, and he likely will not be found guilty of burglary.

(Choice B) A defendant is guilty of attempted burglary if he/she (1) intended to commit burglary, (2) committed an act in furtherance of the burglary, but (3) did not complete it. Legal impossibility is a defense to attempt if the defendant's actions would not constitute a crime even if completed. And since it is legally impossible to unlawfully break and enter a store that is open to the public, the man is not guilty of attempted burglary.

(Choice D) A minority of jurisdictions hold that a person loses his/her status as an invitee when entering an open business with the intent to commit a crime. However, a person retains that status in most jurisdictions (default rule on the MBE). Therefore, the man retained his status as an invitee, despite his intent to rob the store.

📌 Educational Objective

Burglary requires that a breaking and entering be unlawful—ie, without the owner's permission or legal privilege. A business gives the public permission to enter its premises during business hours, but not when it is closed.

在该法域，入室犯法罪（burglary）的定义是“侵入并进入任何建筑物或构筑物，意图在其中实施重罪或盗窃。”

该男子是否可能被判犯有入室犯法罪（burglary）？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该男子有进入便利店的许可。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：入室盗窃（burglary）要求“闯入 + 进入”必须是未经许可的；商店营业中对公众开放，所以进去不等于非法进入。

三秒认题路径：

营业中开放 → 有许可进入 → 非法进入缺失 → burglary 不成 → 选 No

核心法律规则

入室盗窃（burglary）看的是：破门并进入（breaking and entering），而且这一步必须是非法的，也就是没有屋主许可或法律特权。对商店来说，营业时间内对公众开放，顾客有许可进去；关门后才没有这个许可。

所以，哪怕你心里想的是抢劫（robbery），只要你进去时商店还在营业、门也对公众开放，unlawful entry 这道门槛就过不去。

核心判例：本题考的是普通法 burglary 的许可进入规则；营业中商店对公众开放，通常不构成盗窃所需的非法进入。

思维导图

先看：有没有 未经许可的进入？
YES才继续看：是否带着偷窃/重罪意图进入 → 可能成立 burglary。
本题卡死点：商店营业中对公众开放，进入本身是有许可的。
NO直接停：没有非法进入，就没有 burglary；后面的抢劫念头救不了这个罪名。
一句话落点：permission 在手，burglary 先输。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他明明是来抢劫的，还把枪掏出来了，应该算 burglary。

但考试真正问的是：进去那一刻是不是未经许可。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。（这里只是提醒你别把“有坏心”当成“已非法进入”。）

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干关键事实是商店还在营业、对公众开放，所以他进入时有许可；许可进入 一在，burglary 所需的非法进入就没了。

❌ 法律适用 | 轻罪升级误判

✕ B: 把未遂硬套上去，忽略了这一步本来就不是 burglary。

❌ 事实误判 | 闯入条件偷换

✕ C: 只盯着他有偷窃念头，漏看商店仍对公众开放。

❌ 概念混淆 | invitee 规则误套

✕ D: 少数州才会这么看，MBE 默认不因犯意自动失去 invitee 身份。

这题建议用什么方法？

先卡“是否非法进入”，再看主观犯意；入口合法时，后面的坏念头不够把 burglary 拉起来。

考场速记

记忆口诀：先看门能不能合法进，再看你想偷什么。商店营业中对公众开放，通常就不是 burglary；想法再坏，也不能替代非法进入。

看到“开门营业 + 你走进去”，先问一句：这一步有没有 permission？ 没有非法进入，就先排除 burglary。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man admired his coworker's wristwatch and frequently said how much he wished he had one like it. The coworker decided to give the man the watch for his birthday the following week. On the weekend before the man's birthday, the man and the coworker attended a company picnic. The coworker took his watch off and left it on a blanket when he went off to join in a touch football game. The man strolled by, saw the watch on the blanket, and decided to steal it. He bent over and picked up the watch. Before he could pocket it, however, the coworker returned. When the coworker saw the man holding the watch, the coworker said, "I know how much you like that watch. I was planning to give it to you for your birthday. Go ahead and take it now." The man kept the watch.
Which crime has the man committed?

choices.A: Attempted larceny.
choices.B: Embezzlement.
choices.C: Larceny.
choices.D: No crime.

questions.explanation:
Larceny complete
No defense
Man decides to
steal coworker’s
watch
→
Man picks up
watch without
permission
→
Coworker lets
man keep
watch
Intent to
permanently deprive
Unlawful taking &
carrying away

Larceny is the:

  • unlawful taking and carrying away of another's personal property
  • with the specific intent to permanently deprive the owner of that property (ie, intent to steal).

An unlawful taking occurs when the defendant removes the property from the owner's possession and control without consent. Property is carried away as soon as the defendant moves it a short distance (eg, mere inches). And once the defendant has committed larceny, it is no defense that the owner later consented to the taking.

Here, the man grabbed the coworker's watch without his permission (unlawful taking) and picked it up (carrying away) with the intent to steal it. Although the coworker then told the man that he could have the watch, the coworker's consent is not a defense because it was given after the man had committed larceny (Choice D).

(Choice A) Attempted larceny occurs when the defendant (1) possesses the specific intent to steal, (2) commits an overt act in furtherance of the theft, but (3) does not complete it. But here, the man completed the larceny once he bent over and picked up the watch.

(Choice B) Embezzlement requires proof that a person in lawful possession of another's property fraudulently converted it. Lawful possession occurs when a person possesses or controls the property with the owner's permission. Here, the man did not lawfully possess the watch when he picked it up because he did not have the coworker's permission to do so. Therefore, the man did not commit embezzlement.

📌 Educational Objective

Larceny is the (1) unlawful taking and carrying away of another's personal property (2) with the specific intent to permanently deprive the owner of that property. And the owner's consent to the taking after the defendant has completed the larceny does not negate the defendant's criminal liability.

该男子犯了什么罪？

zh-choices.A: 盗窃未遂罪（Attempted larceny）。
zh-choices.B: 侵占罪（Embezzlement）。
zh-choices.C: 盗窃罪（Larceny）。
zh-choices.D: 未犯罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：盗窃罪（larceny）在非法取走并搬离财物时就已经成立，事后失主说“你可以拿走”也救不回去。

三秒认题路径：

想偷 → 伸手拿走 → 已搬离 → 事后同意 → 不免责

核心法律规则

考场上只抓这条规则

盗窃罪（larceny） = 未经同意的取走并搬离（unlawful taking and carrying away） + 永久剥夺意图（intent to permanently deprive）。搬离（carrying away）不需要走很远，抬起、移动几英寸就够了，考场意思：你一旦拿起来准备带走，通常就已经踩线。

而且，事后同意（later consent）不是抗辩；考场意思：盗窃已经做成之后，失主再改口，也不能把已经成立的犯罪“撤销”。

核心判例：Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用本题；本题真正锁定结论的是普通法盗窃规则：取走+搬离+偷的心思一到位，后面再同意也晚了。

思维导图

先看：男人拿手表时，是否已经有偷的意思？
YES 他“决定偷”后，弯腰拿起手表。
规则 非法取走并搬离 + 永久剥夺意图 = 盗窃已成。
卡死点 失主随后说“你可以拿走”也太晚，不能洗白已经完成的盗窃。
排除 不是 attempted larceny，因为他已经拿起并搬离了；也不是 embezzlement，因为他当时根本没有合法占有。
结论 选 C. larceny。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然同事后来明确说“你可以拿走”，那就像是他同意了，应该没犯罪。

但考试真正问的是：同意出现的时间点。这里的同意来得太晚，盗窃在他抬起手表并准备带走时就已经完成了。

司法考试看的是「行为当时能不能成立犯罪」，而不是「后来有没有人心软」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

他在未经许可时已决定偷，并把手表抬起移动，unlawful taking and carrying away已经完成；失主事后同意不影响既成的盗窃。

❌ 概念混淆 | 既遂未分清

✕ A: 把attempted larceny当成答案，但他已经拿起并搬离，早就不是未遂。

❌ 事实误判 | 合法占有偷换

✕ B: 把他当成先合法占有再挪用，但他一开始就没得到允许。

❌ 法律适用 | 事后同意误用

✕ D: 看到Go ahead就以为能免责，但同意来得太晚，救不了已经做成的盗窃。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“拿走时有没有许可”和“当场有没有搬离”，再看事后同意是否来得太晚。

考场速记

记住一句：盗窃先成，后同意无效。看见“他决定偷、拿起、移动”这三步，先锁定 larceny，不要被事后让渡带跑。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A woman and her coworker were invited to go on a hunting trip by their boss. The woman and the coworker were vying for the same promotion, so they were eager to impress their boss with their hunting skills. At one point while the woman and the coworker were hunting alone, the coworker pointed a gun at the woman while her back was turned and said, "Promise you will turn down the promotion or I will shoot you!" Unbeknownst to the coworker, the woman could not hear him because she had placed protective earplugs in her ears before the hunt began. The coworker believed that the woman was intentionally ignoring him, so he aimed at and killed a nearby deer, frightening the woman with the blast from the gun.
If the coworker is charged with assault, is he likely to be convicted?

choices.A: No, because the coworker took no substantial step toward committing a battery.
choices.B: No, because the woman was not aware of the coworker's threat of harm.
choices.C: Yes, because the coworker intended to cause apprehension of bodily harm.
choices.D: Yes, because the woman was placed in actual danger when the coworker pointed the gun at her.

questions.explanation:
There are two types of criminal assault:

  • Attempted battery – when the defendant has the specific intent to commit and takes a substantial step toward committing a battery
  • "Fear of harm" assault (ie, apprehension assault) – when the defendant intentionally places another in reasonable apprehension of imminent harmful or offensive contact

For "fear of harm" assault, the victim must have been aware of the defendant's threat of harm at the time it occurred. Because actual apprehension is necessary, the victim's lack of awareness of the threat of harm is a defense to this type of assault.

Here, the coworker did not intend to batter the woman and took no substantial step toward doing so. He did, however, intend to place the woman in reasonable apprehension of imminent harmful contact (Choice A). But the woman was not aware of the coworker's threat of harm since her back was turned and she could not hear his threat due to her protective earplugs. Therefore, the coworker is not likely to be convicted of assault.

(Choice C) Although the coworker had the requisite intent to cause apprehension of bodily harm, he did not cause the reasonable apprehension of such harm. Both elements must be met for the coworker to be convicted of "fear of harm" assault.

(Choice D) For "fear-of-harm" assault, a defendant need not place a victim in actual danger. Instead, the defendant must intentionally place a victim in reasonable apprehension of harm. Because the woman lacked awareness of the coworker's threat, it is unlikely that the coworker will be convicted of assault.

📌 Educational Objective

Criminal assault occurs when a defendant (1) attempts to commit a battery or (2) intentionally places another in reasonable apprehension of imminent harmful or offensive contact. Apprehension only exists when the person is actually aware of the defendant's threat of harm at the time it occurs.
questions.zh-question:
一名女性和她的同事受老板邀请参加一次狩猎旅行。该女性和她的同事正在竞争同一个晋升机会，因此他们都渴望用自己的狩猎技巧给老板留下深刻印象。在他们两人单独狩猎时，同事在该女性背对着他时用枪指着她，并说：“保证你会拒绝晋升，否则我就开枪打你！”该同事不知道的是，该女性听不到他的话，因为她在狩猎开始前戴上了防护耳塞。该同事认为该女性是故意不理他，于是他瞄准并射杀了一头附近的鹿，枪声吓到了该女性。

如果该同事被控犯有攻击罪(assault)，他是否可能被定罪？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该同事并未采取实质性步骤来实施伤害罪(battery)。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该女性并未意识到同事的伤害威胁。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该同事意图引起对身体伤害的恐惧。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为当同事用枪指着她时，该女性处于实际危险之中。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes Against the Person

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：刑事攻击（criminal assault）里，恐惧型攻击（fear-of-harm assault）必须让受害人当场知道威胁，没意识到就不成立。

三秒认题路径：

枪口指向 → 传达威胁 → 她没听见 → 没有意识 → 不能定罪

核心法律规则

刑事攻击（criminal assault）有两条路：一条是未遂殴打（attempted battery），一条是恐惧型攻击（fear-of-harm assault）。前者看的是想打人并且已经往打人方向走了一大步；后者看的是故意让对方对迫在眉睫的有害或冒犯性接触（imminent harmful or offensive contact）产生合理恐惧。

本题走的是第二条路，所以关键不是“有没有危险”，而是受害人当时有没有真的知道威胁。知悉（awareness）是考试要件：人没听见、没看到、根本不知道威胁，apprehension 就没起来。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用于本题；本题对应的是攻击要件中的“受害人必须知悉威胁”这条规则。

思维导图

先看这是不是恐惧型攻击（fear-of-harm assault）。
第一问：受害人当时知道威胁吗？
没听见、没看到、没意识到 → 这条路直接断掉
第二问：只是让“旁人觉得吓人”够不够？
不够。考试要的是她本人当时对威胁产生apprehension。
第三问：刀枪已经拿出来，为什么还不是自动成立？
因为攻击（assault）不是看画面有多危险，而是看受害人有没有被这一下“吓到”。
结论：她戴着耳塞、背对着他，没意识到威胁 → 不能定攻击（assault）。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他都拿枪对着她了，actual danger 这么明显，应该能定攻击。

但考试真正问的是：她当时有没有知道这句威胁、有没有形成对危险的当场恐惧。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 耳塞 + 背对着 直接说明她没意识到威胁；恐惧型攻击（fear-of-harm assault） 需要当场知悉，所以不能定罪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把攻击硬看成 substantial step 的未遂殴打，路子走错了。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间要件漏掉

✕ C: 只抓“想吓人”不够，没把她真的知道威胁这一步补上。

❌ 事实误判 | 实际危险偷换

✕ D: 把“有危险”偷换成“成立攻击”，actual danger 不是这里的测试点。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是未遂殴打还是恐惧型攻击，再卡死“受害人是否当场知悉威胁”这一关。

考场速记

记忆口诀：攻击（assault）先看“她知不知道”，不是先看“他凶不凶”。这题一眼抓住apprehension，再记住：没意识到威胁，就没有恐惧型攻击。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A woman stole a coat from a coat rack in a restaurant. Several days later, the woman wore the coat on the subway. The subway doors closed on her coat sleeve and nearly tore the sleeve off. The woman took off the coat and threw it into a trash bin at the next subway station. A passerby spotted the coat and retrieved it from the bin. Upon closer examination, the passerby noticed that the sleeve on the coat was torn badly at the seam. Realizing that she could repair and salvage the coat, she took it home and repaired it. Subsequently, when the passerby was wearing the coat in public, the original owner of the coat recognized it and accused the passerby of stealing her coat.
Is the passerby guilty of larceny?

choices.A: No, because the coat was initially stolen by the woman.
choices.B: No, because the passerby believed that the coat had been abandoned.
choices.C: Yes, because the original owner was the rightful owner of the coat.
choices.D: Yes, because the passerby intended to keep the coat when she took it home.

questions.explanation:
Applicability of mistake-of-fact defense

Type of mens rea
Strict liability crime
(eg, statutory rape)
Specific intent
(eg, first-degree murder)
General intent & malice
(eg, involuntary manslaughter)
Never a defense
Honest mistake
negates specific
intent
Honest & reasonable
mistake negates
mens rea

Larceny is the trespassory taking and carrying away (i.e., asportation) of another's personal property with the specific intent to permanently deprive that person of the property (i.e., the intent to steal). But a defendant's belief that the property was abandoned—even if incorrect and unreasonable—serves as a defense to larceny because it negates the intent requirement (i.e., mistake-of-fact defense).

Here, a woman stole a coat and, several days later, threw it into a trash bin at a subway station. A passerby found the coat in the trash bin, took the coat home, and repaired a torn sleeve. Although the original owner of the coat was its rightful owner, the passerby mistakenly believed that the original owner had surrendered her right to the coat by throwing it away in the trash bin. As a result, the passerby lacked the specific intent to steal (Choice C). Therefore, because the passerby believed that the coat had been abandoned, she is not guilty of larceny.

(Choice A) It is irrelevant that the coat was initially stolen by the woman, as this alone is not a defense to larceny for the passerby. This is because larceny can also be committed against a thief. But here, the passerby lacked the requisite intent due to a mistake of fact, so she cannot be found guilty of larceny.

(Choice D) Though the passerby did intend to keep the coat when she took it home, this alone is insufficient to warrant a conviction for larceny. That is because a defendant must also have the specific intent to steal. And here, the passerby lacked such intent, as she honestly believed that the coat had been abandoned by its owner.

📌 Educational Objective

Larceny is the trespassory taking and carrying away of another's personal property with the specific intent to permanently deprive that person of the property. But a defendant's belief that the property was abandoned serves as a defense to larceny because it negates the intent requirement.
questions.zh-question:
一名女子从餐馆的衣帽架上偷了一件外套。几天后，这名女子在地铁上穿着这件外套。地铁门夹住了她的外套袖子，差点把袖子扯掉。这名女子脱下外套，并在下一站把它扔进了垃圾桶。一名路人看到了这件外套，并从垃圾桶里把它捡了出来。经仔细检查后，路人发现外套袖子的接缝处严重撕裂。意识到自己可以修好并保住这件外套后，她把外套带回家并进行了修补。之后，当这名路人在公共场合穿着这件外套时，外套的原所有人认出了它，并指控这名路人偷了她的外套。

这名路人是否构成 larceny（盗窃罪）？

zh-choices.A: 不构成，因为这件外套最初是被那名女子偷走的。
zh-choices.B: 不构成，因为这名路人以为这件外套已被弃置（abandoned）。
zh-choices.C: 构成，因为外套的原所有人才是该外套的合法所有人。
zh-choices.D: 构成，因为这名路人在把外套带回家时就打算保留它。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Theft & receiving stolen goods

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：larceny（盗窃）里，拾得人如果真诚以为财物已经被遗弃，就会因为缺少specific intent（特定故意）而不成立盗窃。

三秒认题路径：

看到扔进垃圾桶 → 先问是否遗弃 → 再看主观认识 → 误信已抛弃 → 不构成盗窃

核心法律规则

这题只用这条规则

larceny（盗窃）要求对他人财物作trespassory taking and carrying away（非法取走并移动），并且要有specific intent（特定故意）去permanently deprive（永久剥夺）他人财物。对这题来说，关键不是原来的 coat 谁先偷的，而是这个路人拿走时，心里是不是在想“这东西已经被主人扔了”。

如果她真诚相信财物已经被abandoned（遗弃），即使这个判断错了，仍然会打掉盗窃所需的故意。考场意思：她不是在“偷别人的东西”，而是在“捡被丢掉的东西”。

核心判例： People v. Graves - 遗弃财物的真诚误信会否掉盗窃所需的特定故意，所以通常不是 larceny。

思维导图

看到“从垃圾桶里拿回外套” → 先问：她拿的时候，主观上是在“捡遗弃物”，还是在“偷别人财物”？
第1步：她是否相信衣物已被主人丢弃？
如果是，specific intent（特定故意）直接被打掉。
第2步：原物主仍是权利人吗？
是，但这只说明“主人没真的放弃权利”，不自动等于她构成盗窃。
结论：只要她诚实相信已经被遗弃，就缺少偷窃故意 → 答案选 B：不构成 larceny

考点陷阱

你可能会想：原始所有人当然还是“真正主人”，所以后来拿走的人也一定在偷。

但考试真正问的是：她拿走那一刻有没有specific intent（特定故意）去偷，而不是物品历史上是不是先被别人偷过。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这里同理，考的是她当时的主观认识，不是外套到底经历过几手。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的trash bin和“她以为外套被扔掉了”直接指向abandoned（遗弃）误信，故缺少盗窃所需的specific intent（特定故意）。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“先前被偷”当成自动成立盗窃，忽略了后手仍要看自己的故意。

❌ 法律适用 | 权利人误导判

✕ C: 只盯着原主人是权利人，没看拾得人当时是不是在想“这是被丢掉的”。

❌ 事实误判 | 保留意图偷换

✕ D: 只看到她想留着外套，漏掉了她是否有“偷”的主观目的。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“遗弃物误信”这个故意阻却点，再回头看是否满足盗窃的特定故意。

考场速记

记忆口诀：看到垃圾桶，先想遗弃；真诚信错，就少故意。 盗窃题别先盯“谁原本是主人”，先问拿的人心里是不是在“偷”。

B.text: believed that the coat had been abandoned

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A bartender asked a woman to spend a weekend with him at his apartment and promised her they would get married on the following Monday. The woman agreed and also promised the bartender that she would not tell anyone of their plans. Unknown to the woman, the bartender had no intention of marrying her.
After the woman came to his apartment, the bartender told her he was going for cigarettes. He called the woman's father and told him that he had his daughter and would kill her if he did not receive $100,000. The bartender was arrested on Sunday afternoon when he went to pick up the $100,000. The woman was still at the apartment and knew nothing of the bartender's attempt to get the money.
Of which crime is the bartender guilty?

choices.A: Kidnapping.
choices.B: Attempted kidnapping.
choices.C: Kidnapping or attempted kidnapping but not both.
choices.D: Neither kidnapping nor attempted kidnapping.

questions.explanation:
Kidnapping
Common law Forcibly abducting or stealing person from his/her own country & sending to another country
MPC Unlawfully moving or confining another to:
  • hold for ransom or as hostage
  • facilitate commission of felony or flight thereafter
  • injure/terrorize victim or another or
  • interfere with governmental/political function
Modern view General Intentional & unlawful confinement involving:
  • some movement (asportation) or
  • concealment
Aggravated General kidnapping committed for:
  • ransom
  • commission of other crime
  • offensive purpose or
  • child stealing
MPC = Model Penal Code.

Under the modern view, kidnapping is (1) the unlawful and intentional confinement of another coupled with (2) the movement or concealment of that person. Confinement occurs when the victim's freedom of movement is restricted against his/her will—ie, by force, threat of force, or deception. As a result, there is no kidnapping if the victim consents to the confinement.

Here, the man convinced the woman to spend the weekend with him by falsely promising to marry her. But his false promise did not restrict the woman to the apartment against her will—she remained there voluntarily. As a result, the man cannot be convicted of kidnapping (Choices A & C). And he cannot be convicted of attempted kidnapping because he (1) never intended to kidnap the woman and (2) did not commit an overt act in furtherance of that crime. Instead, he merely intended to trick the father into paying a $100,000 ransom (Choices B & C).

📌 Educational Objective

Under the modern view, kidnapping is the unlawful and intentional confinement of another that involves the movement or concealment of that person. Since confinement occurs when a person's movement is restricted against his/her will, consent is a defense to kidnapping.
questions.zh-question:
一名酒保邀请一名女子到他的公寓共度周末，并承诺他们将于下周一结婚。该女子同意了，并向酒保承诺她不会将他们的计划告诉任何人。该女子不知道的是，酒保并无意图与她结婚。

女子来到他的公寓后，酒保告诉她他要去买香烟。他打电话给该女子的父亲，告诉他他女儿在他手上，如果收不到10万美元，他就会杀了她。周日下午，当酒保去取这10万美元时被捕。该女子仍在公寓里，对酒保企图获取金钱一事一无所知。

酒保有罪于哪项罪行？

zh-choices.A: 绑架罪。
zh-choices.B: 绑架未遂罪。
zh-choices.C: 绑架罪或绑架未遂罪，但非两者皆是。
zh-choices.D: 既不构成绑架罪，也不构成绑架未遂罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes Against the Person

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：绑架（kidnapping）要有“未得同意的限制自由 + 移动或隐藏”，受害人自愿留下，就不是绑架；而且想判未遂绑架（attempted kidnapping），还得真的朝“把女人绑走”迈出实质步骤，而不是只想骗赎金。

三秒认题路径：

先看同意 → 再看限制自由 → 没有绑人 → 直接排除未遂

核心法律规则

现代观点（modern view）下，绑架要求对他人进行故意且违法的限制，并伴随移动（asportation）或隐藏（concealment）。限制自由（confinement）的关键是受害人是否被against his/her will地关住；如果对方是自愿留下，就没有绑架。

要判未遂（attempt），不仅要有想犯罪的心，还要有朝该罪迈进的实质步骤（overt act）。这题里，bartender 真正想骗的是父亲的赎金，不是先把女人非法带走，所以未遂绑架也不成立。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用；本题对应的是绑架的现代定义与“同意即排除限制自由”的规则。

思维导图

先问：女人是被“关住”的吗？
NO：她是自己答应去公寓的，且没有被强迫留在那儿
→ 没有 confinement，所以直接卡死“绑架”
再问：有没有非法移动或隐藏？
NO：题干只说他去打电话骗赎金，没有把她带走、挪走或藏起来
→ 只有骗钱意图，没有完成绑架的动作链
最后问：能不能改成未遂绑架？
NO：他没有打算绑她，只想让父亲付钱；也没有朝“非法抓人”迈出实质步骤
→ 结论：D，既不是绑架，也不是未遂绑架

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他都威胁要杀人、还索要赎金了，应该就是绑架。

但考试真正问的是：女人有没有被违背意愿地限制自由；这题里她是自愿留下来的，所以“吓人”和“骗赎金”不等于已经绑人。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

女人是自己跟他去公寓的，题干没有against her will的限制自由；他后面只是打电话要赎金，没有完成绑架，也没有朝“绑走她”迈出未遂所需的实质步骤。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把ransom当成自动成立绑架，忽略了她根本没被强迫关住。

❌ 法律适用 | 未遂要件误判

✕ B: 只看到威胁电话，就误以为已经朝绑人迈出实质步骤。

❌ 事实误判 | 自愿同意偷换

✕ C: 把“她自愿留下”偷换成“先绑了再说”，题干事实不支持。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓是否存在非自愿限制自由，再看有没有真正的移动/隐藏，最后才碰未遂。

考场速记

记住：绑架（kidnapping）先看“人有没有被硬留住”，不是先看“有没有赎金”。同意（consent）一成立，限制自由就很难成立。

速记：先问是否被迫留下，再问有没有移动或隐藏；没绑人，就别急着给“绑架”打勾。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A chemistry student manufactured and sold methamphetamine to pay for her college tuition. One day, she mentioned to a friend that state law strictly limits purchases of certain medications used in the production of methamphetamine. Because the student could only purchase a small quantity of these medications at a time, she also mentioned that it would take her until the next semester to acquire enough ingredients to produce her next batch.
That night, the friend asked the student for a ride to a local pharmacy to pick up a few items. Unbeknownst to the student, the friend stole several boxes of the medication that the student needed to make methamphetamine from the pharmacy shelf. The student then drove the friend back to the friend's dorm room.
Later that week, the friend delivered the stolen boxes of medication to the student. When the student asked how the friend had gotten the medication, the friend admitted that she had stolen it from the pharmacy. The student offered to pay the friend for the medication, but the friend said, "Don't worry about it. Friends support each other." The student accepted the medication and started preparing a batch.
On these facts, which of the following crimes has the student committed?

choices.A: Accessory after the fact to larceny.
choices.B: Accomplice to larceny.
choices.C: Conspiracy to commit larceny.
choices.D: Receiving stolen property.

No agreement or encouragement =
