Not an accessory after the fact

Receiving stolen property is a statutory crime that is committed when a person:

  • receives control of stolen personal property
  • knows that the property was stolen (eg, unlawfully obtained through larceny, embezzlement, false pretenses) and
  • specifically intends to permanently deprive the owner of that property.

Here, the student accepted the medication (received control) after the friend admitted that she had stolen it from the pharmacy (knowledge). The student then began preparing a batch of methamphetamine with the stolen medication, indicating her intention to permanently deprive the owner of the medication. Therefore, the student committed the crime of receiving stolen property.

(Choice A) An accessory after the fact is a person who aids or assists a felon in avoiding apprehension or conviction after commission of the felony (eg, larceny). Here, there is no indication that the student did anything to assist the friend in avoiding apprehension or conviction after the friend stole the medication.

(Choice B) An accomplice is a person who (1) intentionally aids or encourages the principal before or during a crime (2) with the specific intent that the crime be completed. Here, the student did assist the friend in carrying away the stolen medication, but she did so unknowingly. Therefore, the student lacked the requisite intent to be an accomplice to larceny.

(Choice C) Conspiracy requires proof that two or more persons entered an agreement with the specific intent to commit a crime. Here, the student and the friend never entered into an agreement to steal medication from the pharmacy before the theft took place. As a result, the student did not conspire to commit larceny.

📌 Educational Objective

Receiving stolen property is committed when a person (1) receives control of stolen personal property, (2) knows that the property was stolen, and (3) specifically intends to permanently deprive the owner of that property.
questions.zh-question:
一名化学专业的学生为了支付大学学费而制造并销售甲基苯丙胺。一天，她向一位朋友提及，州法律严格限制购买某些用于生产甲基苯丙胺的药品。由于该学生每次只能购买少量此类药品，她还提到，她要到下个学期才能获得足够生产下一批产品的原料。

当晚，这位朋友请该学生开车送她去当地一家药店买几样东西。在该学生不知情的情况下，这位朋友从药店货架上偷走了几盒该学生制造甲基苯丙胺所需的药品。随后，该学生开车将朋友送回其宿舍。

当周晚些时候，这位朋友将偷来的几盒药品交给了该学生。当学生问朋友是如何得到这些药品时，朋友承认那是她从药店偷来的。该学生提出要付钱给朋友购买这些药品，但朋友说：“别担心。朋友之间就该互相支持。” 该学生接受了这些药品，并开始准备生产下一批。

根据这些事实，该学生犯了以下哪项罪行？

zh-choices.A: 盗窃罪 (larceny) 的事后从犯。
zh-choices.B: 盗窃罪 (larceny) 的共犯。
zh-choices.C: 共谋实施盗窃罪 (larceny)。
zh-choices.D: 收受赃物罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：拿到明知是偷来的财物后继续占有并使用，构成receiving stolen property（收受赃物），不是去帮偷窃的人脱身。

三秒认题路径：

先偷后给 → 知道是赃物 → 继续收下 → 想据为己有 → 选赃物罪

核心法律规则

收受赃物（receiving stolen property）要看三件事：拿到对方已经偷来的动产、知道（knowledge）它是偷来的、而且还打算自己一直占着用，等于想把原主的东西彻底拿走。

这里最关键的是：学生是在知道真相后才接受控制（receives control）这些药品，还开始用它们做下一批甲基苯丙胺，所以答案直接落在赃物罪。

核心判例：本题按 receiving stolen property 的标准走，不需要额外找共犯关系；知道是赃物后继续收下并使用，就已经够了。

思维导图

看到题干：先偷、后交给学生、学生再知道真相并继续拿着用
第一关：是不是终局前的帮助？
不是，学生是在偷窃完成后才知道并收下药品。
第二关：是不是共谋（conspiracy）？
要先有偷窃前的合意；题干只说她事后才知道，没有 agreement。
第三关：是不是事后从犯（accessory after the fact）？
要帮忙躲警察、躲逮捕；题干没有任何避捕动作。
最后锁定：收受赃物
知道是偷来的 + 接着拿着用 + 想永久占有 → 正确答案 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她一开始还帮朋友把药带回宿舍，好像像accomplice。

但考试真正问的是：她帮忙时根本不知道是偷的，真正成立的是后来明知赃物还继续收下。

这题看的是「事后知道了还要不要收」，不是「一开始有没有无意中帮到」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

学生在知道药品是被偷来的以后仍然接受并使用，已经是控制赃物并打算据为己有，所以构成receiving stolen property。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 她没帮忙躲抓，after the fact 这条线根本没起。

❌ 事实误判 | 事前知情偷换

✕ B: 她偷运时不知情，命题人想骗你把无心帮忙当成故意协助。

❌ 法律适用 | 合意时点误判

✕ C: 题干没有偷窃前合意，agreement 这一关直接空白。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清“事前帮忙”和“事后明知仍占有”，再把共犯、事后从犯和赃物罪分开看。

考场速记

记住一句：先偷后收、知道还拿、想自己用，优先想到receiving stolen property。

如果题目问的是中间上诉，才去记口诀：“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely”——但这题不是程序题，不要乱套。

reason.en: Eliminates accomplice and conspiracy liability because the student had no prior knowledge or intent when the theft occurred.

highlights.text: The student accepted the medication and started preparing a batch

reason.en: Completing all three elements: receipt of control, knowledge of stolen nature, and intent to permanently deprive.
reason.zh: 完成三个构成要件：控制占有、知悉赃物性质、永久剥夺意图。

highlights.text: Friends support each other

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man entered the county museum at a time when it was open to the public, intending to steal an etching by a famous painter. Once inside, he took what he thought was the etching from an unlocked display case and concealed it under his coat. However, the etching was a photocopy of an original that had been loaned to another museum. A sign over the display case containing the photocopy said that similar photocopies were available free at the entrance. The man did not see the sign.
Burglary in the jurisdiction is defined as "entering a building unlawfully with the intent to commit a crime."
Of which crime(s) is the man guilty?

choices.A: Burglary and larceny.
choices.B: Burglary and attempted larceny.
choices.C: Larceny.
choices.D: Attempted larceny.

questions.explanation:
Larceny

(unlawful taking requirement)

In this jurisdiction (and most others), burglary requires proof that a person unlawfully entered a building with the intent to commit a crime therein. Here, the man entered the museum with the intent to steal an etching. But since persons may lawfully enter a building held open to the public, his entry was lawful. Therefore, he is not guilty of burglary (Choices A & B).

However, the man is guilty of larceny—ie, the unlawful (eg, nonconsensual) taking and carrying away of another's personal property with the specific intent to permanently deprive the owner thereof. The man took a photocopy of the etching from the display case even though other copies were available for free at the museum's entrance (unlawful taking). He then completed the crime when he concealed the photocopy under his coat (carrying away) with the intent to steal it (permanent deprivation).

(Choices B & D): Attempt occurs when a person (1) has the specific intent to commit a crime, (2) engages in an act in furtherance of that crime, but (3) does not complete it. Since the man completed the larceny, he is not guilty of attempt.

📌 Educational Objective

Burglary requires proof that a person unlawfully entered a building, so a person cannot burglarize a building while it is open to the public. And larceny requires proof that a person took another's personal property unlawfully—eg, without the owner's consent.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子在县博物馆对公众开放时进入，意图偷窃一幅著名画家的蚀刻画。进入馆内后，他从一个未上锁的陈列柜中取走了他认为是蚀刻画的物品，并将其藏在外套下。然而，该“蚀刻画”是一份影印本，其原作已被借给另一家博物馆。存放该影印本的陈列柜上方有一个标志，说明入口处可免费索取类似的影印本。该男子没有看到这个标志。

在该司法管辖区，入室犯法罪（Burglary）被定义为“以实施犯罪为目的非法进入建筑物”。

该男子犯了何种罪行？

zh-choices.A: 入室犯法罪（Burglary）与盗窃罪（larceny）。
zh-choices.B: 入室犯法罪（Burglary）与盗窃未遂（attempted larceny）。
zh-choices.C: 盗窃罪（Larceny）。
zh-choices.D: 盗窃未遂（Attempted larceny）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：建筑物对公众开放时，进入是合法的，所以不构成 burglary；但偷偷拿走展柜里的复制品，满足 larceny。

三秒认题路径：

公众开放 → 进入合法 → burglary 否 → 偷拿财物 → larceny 是

核心法律规则

入室盗窃（burglary）考场意思：必须是 违法进入（unlawful entry），而不是“带着坏心思进去”就够。一个对公众开放的博物馆，通常允许你进入，所以这一层先卡掉。

盗窃罪（larceny）考场意思：看的是未经同意拿走别人的个人财物，并且有永久剥夺意思；把东西塞进外套里带走，通常就完成了。

如果已经把财物拿走并带离原处，就不是未遂（attempt），而是既遂。

核心判例： 本题按普通法 burglary / larceny 规则判断；关键在于“公众开放”使进入合法，而“偷偷拿走复制品”完成了 larceny。

思维导图

先看 burglary：是否 违法进入（unlawful entry）？
否：博物馆当时 对公众开放，进入本身合法。
卡死 burglary：只带着偷窃意图还不够，必须先有违法进入。
再看 larceny：是否 拿走他人个人财物 并意图永久剥夺？
是：他把展柜里的复制品塞进外套，完成 taking + carrying away。
最后看 attempt：有没有 not complete？
没有：既然 larceny 已完成，就不是 attempted larceny。
答案落点：只有 C. larceny。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他一开始就是来偷画的，所以 burglary 和 attempted larceny 都该算上。

但考试真正问的是：他进门那一步是不是违法、以及偷拿这一步有没有完成。 这题里博物馆对公众开放，所以进入合法；而复制品已经被他拿走并藏进外套，larceny 不是未遂。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 拿走并藏入外套 已完成 unlawful taking 和 carrying away，所以构成 larceny；但公开开放的博物馆入口不算 burglary 的违法进入。

❌ 概念混淆 | 入口合法误判

✕ A: 把“有偷窃意图”直接当成 burglary。

❌ 法律适用 | 未遂套错题

✕ B: 看到 attempted 就忘了 larceny 已经做完。

❌ 事实误判 | 漏读既遂

✕ D: 把“藏进外套”漏看成还没拿走。

这题建议用什么方法？

先拆 burglary 的进入是否合法，再看 larceny 是否已完成，最后才判断 attempt。

考场速记

记住一句：公众开放 = 进入合法，所以 burglary 先掉；拿走 + 带离 + 永久剥夺意思 一成立，larceny 就完成。

本题口诀：先问“能不能算 unlawful entry”，再问“是不是已经把东西拿走并藏起来”。

reason.en: Lawful entry negates the 'unlawful entry' element required for burglary.
reason.zh: 合法进入否定了入室盗窃所需的'非法进入'要件。

label.zh: 入室盗窃的非法进入要件

reason.en: The statutory definition makes unlawful entry an essential element of burglary.
reason.zh: 法定定义将非法进入作为入室盗窃的必要要件。

reason.en: Concealment completes the carrying-away element of larceny.
reason.zh: 藏匿行为完成了盗窃罪的'带走'要件。

label.en: owner's lack of consent — unlawful taking
label.zh: 所有人未同意——非法取走

reason.en: Free copies at the entrance show the man bypassed the lawful channel, making his taking nonconsensual.
reason.zh: 入口处免费提供副本，说明被告绕过了合法途径，其取走行为属于未经同意的非法占有。

label.en: lack of knowledge — no consent defense

reason.en: Ignorance of the free-copy sign does not negate the unlawful nature of his taking.
reason.zh: 不知道免费副本标志并不能否定其取走行为的非法性。

reason.en: Incorrectly adds burglary when entry was lawful because museum was open to public.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A 22-year-old man went to a nightclub with a group of friends. The nightclub is known for its strict 18-and-up policy. While there, the man ran into a former coworker who introduced the man to her sister. Over the course of the night, the man and the sister danced and engaged in conversation. The sister told the man that she was 19 years old and attended the local university. Near closing time, the sister invited the man to her apartment. Unbeknownst to him, the sister was only 16 and had gotten into the club using a fake ID. Later that evening, the man had consensual sexual intercourse with the coworker's sister.
The age of consent in the jurisdiction is 17.
Is the man guilty of statutory rape?

choices.A: No, because the man did not knowingly engage in sexual intercourse with a minor.
choices.B: No, because the man's mistake of fact, under the totality of circumstances, was reasonable.
choices.C: Yes, because the man was negligent in failing to confirm the sister's age.
choices.D: Yes, because the man's commission of the requisite actus reus is sufficient for a finding of guilt.

questions.explanation:
Applicability of mistake-of-fact defense
Type of mens rea
Strict liability crime
(eg, statutory rape)
Never a defense
Specific intent
(eg, first-degree murder)
Honest mistake negates specific intent
General intent & malice
(eg, involuntary manslaughter)
Honest & reasonable mistake negates mens rea

Statutory rape arises when a defendant has sexual intercourse with a person under the age of consent. This is a strict liability crime, which means that it has no mens rea requirement. Instead, proof of the actus reus (here, intercourse with an underage person) is alone sufficient to support a conviction. As a result, the fact that the man did not knowingly engage in sexual intercourse with a minor does not absolve him of guilt (Choice A).

Additionally, mistake of fact is never a defense to a strict liability crime because this defense is predicated on the notion that the defendant's mistake negates the mens rea necessary to convict. So even though the coworker's sister misrepresented her age to the man, he cannot escape liability for statutory rape by establishing that he was reasonably mistaken about the victim's age (Choice B). Therefore, the man is guilty of statutory rape.

(Choice C) The man did not confirm the sister's age. But whether his failure to do so was negligent—or even reasonable—is irrelevant to this strict liability crime. All that matters is whether he committed the actus reus.

📌 Educational Objective

Mistake of fact is never a defense to a strict liability crime—including statutory rape. Therefore, a defendant's reasonable mistake as to the victim's age will not serve as a defense to statutory rape.
questions.zh-question:
一名22岁的男子和一群朋友去了一家夜店。这家夜店以其严格的18岁及以上准入政策而闻名。在那里，该男子遇到了一位前同事，前同事将她的妹妹介绍给了该男子。在当晚，该男子和这位妹妹一起跳舞、交谈。这位妹妹告诉该男子她19岁，就读于本地大学。临近营业结束时，妹妹邀请该男子去她的公寓。他不知道的是，这位妹妹只有16岁，是使用假身份证进入夜店的。当天晚上晚些时候，该男子与前同事的妹妹发生了双方自愿的性交行为。

在该司法管辖区，法定同意年龄是17岁。

该男子是否构成法定强奸罪 (statutory rape)？

zh-choices.A: 不构成，因为该男子并未在知情的情况下与未成年人发生性交行为。
zh-choices.B: 不构成，因为根据整体情况来看，该男子对事实的错误认知是合理的。
zh-choices.C: 构成，因为该男子在未能确认妹妹年龄方面存在过失。
zh-choices.D: 构成，因为该男子实施了必要的犯罪行为 (actus reus)，足以认定其有罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Rape and Other Sex Crimes

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：法定强奸（statutory rape）是否属于严格责任犯罪（strict liability crime），以及事实错误（mistake of fact）能不能当抗辩。

三秒认题路径：

未成年性交 → 严格责任 → 无需故意 → 事实错误无效 → 选 D

核心法律规则

〈span class="term">法定强奸（statutory rape）只要证明被告与未达同意年龄的人发生性交即可，重点看的是客观行为（actus reus），不是他心里知不知道对方未成年。

因为它是严格责任犯罪（strict liability crime），所以不用证明mens rea；考试上这就表示，哪怕被害人撒谎、被告“合理误信”，通常也挡不住定罪。

事实错误（mistake of fact）只有在需要 mens rea 的题里才可能救人；对严格责任罪，它直接没用。

核心判例： 无特定判例名 - 本题按 MBE 常规规则处理：法定强奸是严格责任，年龄误认不能抗辩。

思维导图

先看：这题是不是要找 mens rea？
是严格责任罪？法定强奸（statutory rape）= 直接看性交 + 未达同意年龄
还要问故意吗？不用，actus reus 一成立就够。
所以“我不知道她 16 岁”也救不了。
再看：mistake of fact 能不能挡？
若是故意犯/一般故意犯： 可能有用。
若是严格责任罪： 无论合理与否，都不能洗掉责任
落点：题干只要证明谁和谁发生了性交？
22 岁男子 + 16 岁女孩 + 自愿性交 + 法定同意年龄 17。
结论：定罪成立，选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她撒了fake ID，而且他看起来也算被“骗”了，所以不该有罪。

但考试真正问的是：这题是不是严格责任犯罪（strict liability crime）；如果是，事实错误（mistake of fact）就不是出口。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这里的“合理相信”很像人情上能理解，但刑法题只认规则：年龄不到，就够了。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干已经给出16 岁与发生性交，法定强奸只看这两个点；它是严格责任罪，所以不需要再证明他知道对方未成年。

❌ 概念混淆 | 故意要件误判

✕ A: 把knowingly当成必要要件了。

❌ 法律适用 | 合理错误误判

✕ B: 以为reasonable 误信能挡严格责任。

❌ 事实误判 | 过失门槛误判

✕ C: 把没确认年龄当成定罪关键。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认罪名是否严格责任，再看事实错误能不能进场，别被“她骗了我”带跑。

考场速记

记住这句：严格责任罪先看行为，不看心里；所以法定强奸里，年龄误认通常不是抗辩。

如果题目在问中间上诉，就背口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely；但这题不是上诉题，核心仍是“未成年 + 性交 = 够了”。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man revered a famous guitarist who had recently died. The man convinced his girlfriend, who worked at the cemetery where the guitarist was buried, to help him acquire a 12-foot sculpture of a steel guitar that had been commissioned by the guitarist's surviving spouse and installed on the guitarist's gravesite. One day, when the girlfriend knew that no other cemetery employees would be present, she gave the man the keys to a truck with a hydraulic lift that the cemetery used to install headstones. She and the man then drove to the guitarist's gravesite. The girlfriend maintained a lookout while the man severed the sculpture from its base and raised it onto the truck bed using the hydraulic lift. The man then drove the sculpture to a storage unit he had rented, placed it in the unit, and returned the truck to the cemetery. On the way home from the storage facility, the man was killed in a car accident.
The police later ascertained the identities of the man and the girlfriend and recovered the sculpture unharmed.
If the girlfriend is charged with larceny in a jurisdiction that follows the common law, which of the following is her best defense?

choices.A: The man, who is deceased, cannot be convicted of larceny.
choices.B: The sculpture constituted real property.
choices.C: The sculpture was unharmed.
choices.D: The taking occurred during the day.

questions.explanation:
At common law, a person who (1) aided or encouraged a principal in the commission of a crime and (2) was present at the crime is classified as a principal in the second degree. This designation is significant because a principal in the second degree is liable for the offense to the same extent as the principal—even if the principal is not convicted.

Here, the girlfriend aided the man in the unlawful removal of the sculpture from the guitarist's grave by serving as a lookout during the removal. As a result, the girlfriend is a principal in the second degree and can be tried and potentially convicted even though the man, who died before police could apprehend him, was not previously convicted (Choice A). For the girlfriend to be convicted of common law larceny, the prosecution must prove that the man:

  • unlawfully took and carried away another's personal property and
  • did so with the intent to permanently deprive the owner of that property.

However, a person who unlawfully severs and then immediately carries away an item of real property—eg, a planted tree or fixture—is not guilty of common law larceny. That is because such an item does not constitute personal property in its attached state.* Therefore, the girlfriend's best defense is that the sculpture affixed to the grave constituted real property and, as such, was not subject to common law larceny.

*In contrast, an item of real property that (1) was previously severed by the owner or (2) was severed by the defendant and later came into the owner's possession is personal property and subject to larceny.

(Choice C) It is not a defense to larceny that the stolen property was recovered unharmed.

(Choice D) Unlike common law burglary, larceny need not be committed at night.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant who unlawfully severs and then immediately carries away an item of real property is not guilty of larceny because such an item does not constitute personal property.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子十分崇敬一位最近去世的著名吉他手。该男子说服了在吉他手安葬的墓地工作的女友，帮助他获取一座12英尺高的钢制吉他雕塑。该雕塑由吉他手在世的配偶委托制作并安装在吉他手的墓地上。一天，女友知道没有其他墓地员工在场，便将墓地用来安装墓碑的、带液压升降机的卡车钥匙交给了该男子。随后，她和该男子开车前往吉他手的墓地。女友负责望风，而该男子则将雕塑从其基座上切断，并用液压升-降机将其吊上卡车车厢。该男子随后将雕塑运至他租来的一个储物单元，将其放入单元内，并将卡车归还至墓地。在从仓储设施回家的路上，该男子在一场车祸中丧生。

警方后来查明了该男子和女友的身份，并找回了完好无损的雕塑。

如果女友在一个遵循普通法（common law）的司法管辖区被控盗窃罪（larceny），以下哪项是她最好的辩护理由？

zh-choices.A: 该男子已故，不能被判定犯有盗窃罪（larceny）。
zh-choices.B: 该雕塑构成不动产。
zh-choices.C: 该雕塑完好无损。
zh-choices.D: 拿取行为发生在白天。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：共犯身份不救你，关键还是看被拿走的东西在“拿走那一刻”是不是 个人财产（personal property）；如果是附着在墓地上的 不动产（real property），共同常法 盗窃（larceny） 就卡住了。

三秒认题路径：

共犯在场 → 共同盗窃 → 先看财产属性 → 附着物被切走 → 不是盗窃

核心法律规则

共同常法盗窃（common law larceny） 要求被拿走的是别人的 个人财产（personal property），并且行为人有 永久剥夺意图（intent to permanently deprive）。如果物品原本是附着在土地上的 不动产（real property），比如墓碑、雕塑、栽种的树，直接 切离并立刻带走（sever and carry away） 时，通常还不算盗窃，因为它在附着状态下还不是可被盗窃的个人财产。

这里 girlfriend 虽然是现场 从犯/次要正犯（principal in the second degree），但她能不能被定盗窃，仍然取决于主行为是否构成盗窃。她的胜点不在“男友后来死了”，而在“这尊雕塑在被切走时还是墓地上的不动产”。

核心判例： 这题对应的是 common law larceny 的附着物规则：sever and immediately carry away 的不动产，一般不算可被盗窃的个人财产。

思维导图

先问：拿走的是不是 个人财产（personal property）？
不是
雕塑原本固定在墓地上，切下瞬间还是 不动产（real property） → common law larceny 卡死
所以 girlfriend 的最佳抗辩：目标物根本不满足盗窃客体
再看：共犯身份能不能救检方？
不能替代要件
她是现场帮忙的人，身份上可以被追责；但如果主行为不构成 larceny，她也不能凭空变出一个盗窃。
答案落点
B
“雕塑构成不动产”直接切断 common law larceny 的客体要件。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：男友已经把雕塑运走了，而且 girlfriend 还负责望风，所以当然是盗窃。

但考试真正问的是：这个物在被拿走那一刻，能不能算 personal property。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的东西有没有被拿走」；这里真正卡住的是财产属性，不是结果有没有追回。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干最关键的事实是雕塑被 从墓地上切下后立刻运走，它在附着状态下还是 不动产（real property），所以不满足 common law larceny 的客体要件。

❌ 概念混淆 | 共犯可罚误判

✕ A: 把“男友死了”当成免死金牌，忽略 girlfriend 仍可单独受追责。

❌ 事实误判 | 无损归还误判

✕ C: 看到 recovered unharmed 就以为无罪，题目根本不看追回结果。

❌ 法律适用 | 夜间要件误判

✕ D: 把 night 这个 burglary 规则硬搬到 larceny。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓客体要件，再看共犯身份；只要是附着物被当场切走，就先怀疑不是 larceny。

考场速记

记住这句：先看是不是 个人财产（personal property），再谈有没有 盗窃（larceny）。 附着在地上的东西，sever and immediately carry away 时先别急着判盗窃；先问它切下那一刻是不是还只是 不动产（real property）。

reason.zh: 将夜间入室盗窃罪的时间要素与盗窃罪混淆，盗窃罪没有时间限制。

highlights.text: installed on the guitarist's gravesite

reason.en: Shows that the sculpture was a fixture annexed to the realty, making it real property.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
An elderly woman was visiting a friend in a sizeable nursing home. After the woman's visit, she attempted to leave the facility. However, a nurse mistakenly believed that the woman was one of the residents and told her to remain on the premises. The woman protested and tried to explain that she was actually a visitor, but the nurse did not believe her. Instead, the nurse guided the woman toward an empty room and told her to wait there until he could verify her identity. The woman refused to enter the room, so the nurse pulled out a syringe and said, "Do I need to give you a sedative or are you going to listen to me?" The woman reluctantly entered the room, and the nurse told the woman to stay in there until he got back. He then closed the door behind him but did not lock it. Thirty minutes later, the nurse returned, apologized for the misunderstanding, and told the woman that she could leave. The woman subsequently filed a criminal complaint against the nurse, and he was charged with false imprisonment.
Is the nurse guilty of false imprisonment?

choices.A: No, because the nurse mistakenly believed that the woman was a patient.
choices.B: No, because the woman was free to leave the unlocked room.
choices.C: Yes, because the nurse intended to lawfully confine a patient, not a visitor.
choices.D: Yes, because the woman's consent was not freely given.

questions.explanation:
Elements of false imprisonment
• Unlawful – not consented to or specifically authorized by law
• Confinement – forcing person to go or remain where person does not wish when no alternative routes are available
• Without consent – not freely agreed to by someone with capacity to do so

False imprisonment is the unlawful confinement of a person without consent. A confinement occurs when a person is compelled through actual force, threat of force, or a show of force to either

  • go where the person does not want to go or
  • remain where the person does not want to remain.

The confinement is unlawful unless it is specifically authorized by law or consented to by the victim. However, consent is only effective if it was freely given (ie, without force or fraud) and the victim had the capacity to consent.

Here, the elderly woman was confined when the nurse threatened to give the woman a sedative unless she entered the room. Although the woman subsequently agreed to enter, her actions did not constitute consent because her compliance was not freely given—it was made in response to the nurse's threat of force. Therefore, the confinement was unlawful.

However, mistake of fact is a defense to false imprisonment and other general intent crimes—which require only the intent to perform an act that is unlawful—if the mistake was honest and reasonable and negates the requisite mens rea. The mens rea required for false imprisonment is the intent to unlawfully confine another.

Here, the nurse may have honestly and reasonably believed that the elderly woman was a resident. But mistake of fact is not a defense because the nurse could not have threatened and confined a nursing home resident in that manner. Such confinement would have also been unlawful. Therefore, the mistake does not negate the requisite mens rea and the nurse is guilty of false imprisonment (Choices A & C).

(Choice B) Although the door was left unlocked, the woman was still confined because she remained in the room due to the nurse's threat of force.

📌 Educational Objective

False imprisonment is the unlawful confinement of a person without consent. Consent is effective only if the victim gave it freely and had the capacity to consent. Mistake of fact is a defense to this general intent crime only if the mistake was honest and reasonable.
questions.zh-question:
一位年长妇女正在一家规模相当大的疗养院探望朋友。探望结束后，该妇女试图离开该设施。然而，一名护士误以为该妇女是院内的一名居民，并告知她必须留在院内。该妇女提出抗议，并试图解释她实际上是一名访客，但护士不相信她。于是，护士将该妇女引导至一个空房间，并告诉她在那里等待，直到他能核实她的身份。该妇女拒绝进入房间，于是护士拿出一个注射器说：“我是需要给你注射一针镇静剂，还是你准备听我的话？”该妇女不情愿地进入了房间，护士告诉她待在里面等他回来。随后，他关上了身后的门，但没有上锁。三十分钟后，护士回来了，为误会道歉，并告诉该妇女可以离开了。该妇女随后对护士提起了刑事诉讼，护士被指控犯有非法拘禁罪（false imprisonment）。

该护士是否犯有非法拘禁罪（false imprisonment）？

zh-choices.A: 不构成，因为护士误以为该妇女是一名病人。
zh-choices.B: 不构成，因为该妇女可以自由离开未上锁的房间。
zh-choices.C: 构成，因为护士的意图是合法地约束一名病人，而非一名访客。
zh-choices.D: 构成，因为该妇女的同意并非自由作出。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes Against the Person

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：非法监禁（false imprisonment）里，同意（consent）是不是“被威胁出来的”，以及“门没锁”会不会洗掉已经发生的强迫拘禁。

三秒认题路径：

威胁上镇静剂 → 逼进房间 → 门没锁也算拘禁 → 同意不自由 → 选 D

核心法律规则

这题只看这条规则

非法监禁（false imprisonment）的核心是：未经同意、且非法地限制他人行动自由。拘禁（confinement）不要求上锁，只要用实际力量、威胁，或明显的强迫，让对方去不想去的地方，或留在不想待的地方，就够了。

同意（consent）只有在“自愿给出”而且有能力同意时才有效；被“给我打镇静剂，不然就怎样”逼出来的配合，不算自由同意，所以仍然是非法拘禁。

错误事实抗辩（mistake of fact）在这里也救不了被告，因为这类题看的是他有没有意图去做“违法拘禁”，而不是他主观上以为对方是不是病人。

核心判例： 本题没有必须点名的判例；考试就记住 威胁逼入房间 + 门没锁不等于能走，足够成立非法监禁。

思维导图

先问：有没有 拘禁（confinement）？
有：护士掏出针筒，威胁“要不要给你打镇静剂”，患者因此进屋并被要求待着。
关键卡点：effectively reviewable 这里不重要；本题要看的是“是否被迫留下”。
再问：这个“同意”算不算真同意？
不算：配合是因为威胁，不是自由选择，所以 without consent 成立。
最后问：门没锁能不能推翻拘禁？
不能：门没锁，但她不敢走，是被威胁留在房间里。
结论：答案 D，因为“被威胁后的配合”不是自由同意。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：门没有上锁，所以女人随时能走，怎么还算拘禁。

但考试真正问的是：她是不是因为护士的威胁才留下来，不是看门锁有没有扣上。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

换句话说，unlocked 不等于 free to leave；只要人是被迫待着，拘禁就已经发生。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 掏出针筒并威胁打镇静剂，让她在压力下进屋并留下，说明同意不是自由给出的，所以非法监禁成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 身份误认错因

✕ A: 把“误认她是病人”当成免责理由，但真正决定结果的是后面的威胁拘禁。

❌ 事实误判 | 门没锁误读

✕ B: 只盯着 unlocked，漏看她是因为威胁才待在房间里。

❌ 法律适用 | 故意对象误套

✕ C: 把“想合法关住病人”当成抗辩，但他实际做的是威胁下的非法拘禁。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“有没有威胁导致人留下”，再看同意是否自由，最后别被门锁状态带跑。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“威胁一出，门没锁也能成立拘禁；同意若是被逼出来的，就不是同意。”

再记一句：false imprisonment 看的是“能不能自由走”，不是“门有没有锁”。

question_analysis.skill_tested: evaluating consent and confinement elements

reason.en: Triggers the need to analyze whether mistake of fact defends false imprisonment.
reason.zh: 触发分析事实错误是否可作为非法拘禁的抗辩理由。

reason.en: Indicates physical force or threat of force used to restrict movement.
reason.zh: 表明用于限制行动的物理暴力或暴力威胁。

reason.en: Presents a potential distraction regarding the definition of confinement.
reason.zh: 针对限制人身自由的定义提供了一个潜在的干扰项。

reason.en: Identifies the core criminal charge being analyzed.
reason.zh: 明确被分析的核心刑事指控。

A.text: mistakenly believed that the woman was a patient

reason.en: Fails because mistake of fact is not a defense if the intended conduct would still be unlawful.
reason.zh: 由于即使意图实施的行为仍属违法，事实错误抗辩在此不成立。

B.text: free to leave the unlocked room

label.zh: 不存在限制人身自由干扰项

reason.en: Ignores that confinement can be achieved via threats of force despite an unlocked door.
reason.zh: 忽略了尽管门未锁，通过暴力威胁同样可以构成人身限制。

C.text: intended to lawfully confine a patient, not a visitor

reason.zh: 错误地假设护士在此种情况下有法律授权去限制病人的自由。

reason.en: Correctly states that compliance obtained by a threat of force does not constitute valid consent.
reason.zh: 正确指出通过暴力威胁获得的顺从不构成有效同意。

highlights.text: mistakenly believed that the woman was one of the residents

reason.en: Triggers the mistake of fact analysis regarding nursing home status.
reason.zh: 触发了关于养老院人员身份的事实错误分析。

highlights.text: Do I need to give you a sedative or are you going to listen to me?

reason.en: The critical threat that overrides voluntary consent and establishes unlawful confinement.
reason.zh: 推翻自愿同意并确立非法限制的关键威胁。

highlights.text: but did not lock it

reason.en: Tests the rule that physical locking is not required when confinement is maintained by threat.
reason.zh: 测试了当通过威胁维持限制时，不需要物理上锁的规则。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A new gang member, hoping to impress the gang's leader, pointed a gun at a pedestrian and ordered her to give him her expensive watch, which she did. The gang member then tossed the watch to the gang leader, who was standing nearby. Although totally surprised by this act, the gang leader put the watch in his pocket. The pedestrian ran away.
What crime did the gang leader commit?

choices.A: Accessory after the fact to robbery.
choices.B: Accomplice to robbery.
choices.C: Conspiracy to commit robbery.
choices.D: Receiving stolen property.

questions.explanation:
The crime of receiving stolen property is committed when a person:

  • receives property that he/she knows was stolen
  • with the intent to permanently deprive another of that property.

Here, the gang leader knew that the watch was stolen since he witnessed the robbery—ie, the gang member's theft of the woman's watch through force or intimidation. The gang member then tossed the watch to the gang leader, who pocketed it—evidencing his intent to permanently deprive the woman of the watch. Therefore, the gang leader committed the crime of receiving stolen property.

(Choice A) An accessory after the fact is a person who aids or assists another (ie, the principal) by helping the principal avoid apprehension or conviction after the crime has been completed. Here, the gang leader did not play this role since his concealment of the watch did not help the gang member in such a manner.

(Choice B) An accomplice (1) knowingly aids or encourages the principal before or during a crime (2) with the intent that the crime be completed. Here, the gang leader was not an accomplice since the gang member acted of his own accord (ie, without aid or encouragement) to impress the gang leader.

(Choice C) Conspiracy is an agreement between two or more people to commit a crime that is entered with the intent to accomplish that crime. Since the gang leader was totally surprised by the gang member's act, they did not agree to commit the robbery.

📌 Educational Objective

The crime of receiving stolen property is committed when a person (1) receives property that he/she knows was stolen (2) with the intent to permanently deprive another of that property.
questions.zh-question:
一名新的黑帮成员，为了给黑帮头目留下深刻印象，用枪指着一名行人，并命令她交出其昂贵的手表，她照做了。该黑帮成员随后将手表扔给了站在附近的黑帮头目。尽管对这一行为感到十分惊讶，该黑帮头目还是将手表放进了自己的口袋。该行人跑走了。

该黑帮头目犯了什么罪？

zh-choices.A: 抢劫罪的事后从犯。
zh-choices.B: 抢劫罪的共犯。
zh-choices.C: 共谋抢劫罪。
zh-choices.D: 收受赃物罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：看到别人刚抢来的财物后，自己接手并据为己有，算不算接收赃物（receiving stolen property）。

三秒认题路径：

知道是偷来的 → 接手财物 → 想占为己有 → 不是帮逃跑 → 选接收赃物

核心法律规则

接收赃物（receiving stolen property），考场意思：你拿到的是“已被偷的东西”，而且你知道它是偷来的。

还要有占有后继续据为己有的意思，也就是有 intent to permanently deprive。这题里，头目亲眼看见抢劫经过，所以知道手表是赃物；他把表塞进口袋，正好说明他不是临时碰一下，而是要留下来。

核心判例： 题目未给出特定判例；按通行 MBE 规则，知道是赃物 + 打算据为己有，就锁定本罪。

思维导图

先看头目是不是“接手赃物的人”
事实：小弟持枪抢表后，立刻把表扔给头目。
关卡 1：头目当场看见抢劫经过 → 知道是偷来的。
关卡 2：头目把表放进口袋 → 据为己有 的意思成立。
卡死点：这不是“帮小弟逃跑”，而是“收下赃物自己留着”。
结论：满足 receiving stolen property → 选 D
别混淆：不需要他先参与抢劫，也不需要和小弟事先商量。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：头目是“事后收东西”，是不是 accessory after the fact。

但考试真正问的是：他收下手表后，是不是自己把赃物留下来，而不是去帮小弟躲警察。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这里同理，考的是“是否接收并据为己有”，不是“是否替别人善后”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

头目亲眼看见抢劫，所以知道手表是赃物；他把表放进口袋，说明有据为己有的意思，正中 receiving stolen property。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 你把收赃物误看成帮逃跑了。

❌ 法律适用 | 事前帮助误判

✕ B: 题干没写头目事先鼓励或协助before or during。

❌ 事实误判 | 事先同意偷换

✕ C: 头目是“突然被扔表”，不是事前商量抢劫。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“知道是赃物”再看“有没有留下来自己用”，不要被事后出现的身份标签带跑。

考场速记

记忆口诀：知道是偷来的 + 收下自己留，就是接收赃物；别把“事后拿到东西”自动等同于“事后帮忙脱罪”。

reason.en: Negates the agreement element of conspiracy and the prior intent element of accomplice liability.

reason.zh: 表明实际收受了被盗财产并具有永久剥夺的意图。

reason.en: The leader's pocketing of the watch did not assist the principal in avoiding apprehension.
reason.zh: 首领将手表放入兜内的行为并未协助主犯逃避逮捕。

reason.en: The leader did not aid, abet, or encourage the gang member before or during the robbery.
reason.zh: 首领在抢劫事前或事中均未提供协助、教唆或鼓励。

reason.en: There was no agreement to commit the robbery because the leader was surprised by the act.
reason.zh: 由于首领对该行为感到意外，因此不存在实施抢劫的合意。

reason.en: Applies because the leader accepted a known stolen item with intent to keep it.
reason.zh: 适用此罪，因为首领在明知是赃物的情况下予以收受并意图占有。

highlights.text: pointed a gun at a pedestrian and ordered her to give him her expensive watch

reason.en: Establishes that the property was acquired via robbery (and is thus stolen property).
reason.zh: 确立了财产是通过抢劫获取的（因此属于赃物）。

highlights.text: Although totally surprised by this act

label.en: negation of prior intent and agreement

reason.en: Defeats accomplice and conspiracy liability due to lack of prior intent or agreement.
reason.zh: 因缺乏事前意图或合意，从而排除了共犯与共谋责任。

highlights.text: put the watch in his pocket

reason.en: Establishes physical receipt of the watch and intent to permanently deprive.
reason.zh: 确立了实际收受手表以及永久剥夺的意图。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man who had become very drunk left a bar and started to walk home. Another patron of the bar, who had observed the man's condition, followed him. The patron saw the man stumble and fall to the ground near an alley. The patron then began to pull out a gun but saw that the man had passed out in the gutter. The patron reached into the man's pocket, grabbed his wallet, and started to walk away. When the patron heard police officers approaching, he dropped the wallet and ran off.
The crimes below are listed in descending order of seriousness.
What is the most serious crime of which the patron properly could be convicted?

choices.A: Robbery.
choices.B: Larceny.
choices.C: Attempted robbery.
choices.D: Attempted larceny.

questions.explanation:
A defendant can be convicted of larceny if he/she:

  • unlawfully took and carried away the victim's property (even a short distance)
  • with the intent to permanently deprive the victim of that property (ie, intent to steal).

And the defendant can be convicted of the more serious crime of robbery if the property was taken from the victim's person or presence by force or intimidation. But if these (or any other) crimes are not completed, the defendant can be convicted of the less serious crime of attempt if he/she:

  • specifically intended to commit the crime and
  • performed an act in furtherance of the crime.

Here, the elements of larceny were met when the patron intentionally took a wallet from the man's pocket and started to walk away. And though the patron later dropped the wallet when he heard the police approaching, this is no defense. Therefore, the patron can be convicted of larceny—not attempted larceny (Choice D).

The patron likely intended to commit robbery when he followed the man and pulled out a gun in furtherance of the crime. But since the man then passed out in the gutter, the patron was able to take the wallet without using force or intimidation. As a result, the patron could be convicted of attempted robbery—but not a completed robbery (Choice A). Nevertheless, larceny is the most serious crime of which the patron could be convicted (Choice C).

📌 Educational Objective

Larceny evolves into the more serious crime of robbery when the defendant takes property from the victim's person or presence by force or intimidation. But if an element of those (or any other) crimes is not completed, a defendant may be convicted of a less serious attempted crime.
questions.zh-question:
一名酩酊大醉的男子离开酒吧，开始步行回家。酒吧的另一名顾客观察到该男子的状况后，便尾随其后。该顾客看到该男子跌跌撞撞，在一条小巷附近摔倒在地。该顾客随后开始拔枪，但看到该男子已在排水沟中昏倒。该顾客伸手到该男子的口袋里，抓住他的钱包，然后开始走开。当该顾客听到警察走近时，他扔下钱包逃跑了。

以下罪行按严重程度降序排列。

该顾客可能被恰当定罪的最严重的罪行是什么？

zh-choices.A: 抢劫罪。
zh-choices.B: 盗窃罪。
zh-choices.C: 抢劫未遂。
zh-choices.D: 盗窃未遂。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：先看是否已经完成 盗窃（larceny），再看 抢劫（robbery） 里的“暴力或恐吓”要件是否真的成立。

三秒认题路径：

偷走钱包 → 先看盗窃 → 再看抢劫 → 没暴力/恐吓 → 选 B

核心法律规则

只抓本题用得上的规则

盗窃（larceny） 要看两件事：非法拿走并带走别人的财物，且 永久剥夺（intent to permanently deprive） 的意思要成立。抢劫（robbery） 则是在此基础上，财物必须从受害人 人身或近旁（person or presence） 被 暴力或恐吓（force or intimidation） 拿走，所以没有这一步，就别硬升格成抢劫。

如果前面已经把财物拿到手，后面又慌忙丢掉，通常不把已经完成的 盗窃（larceny） 变回 未遂（attempt）。这题里，钱包已经从口袋里被拿出并带走，盗窃先完成了。

核心判例： 本题考的是普通法盗窃/抢劫规则，不靠特定判例展开；结论锁定在“先完成盗窃、但没完成抢劫”。

思维导图

先问：抢劫（robbery） 成了吗？
NO 受害人已昏倒在路边，钱包是直接从口袋拿走，不是靠当场 暴力或恐吓（force or intimidation） 拿到。
卡死点：第三步“暴力/恐吓”没过，所以不是抢劫。
再问：盗窃（larceny） 成了吗？
YES 非法伸手进口袋、拿出钱包、开始带走，已经完成“拿走并带离”。
YES 事后听到警察才丢下钱包，不会抹掉已经完成的盗窃。
结论：最高只能到哪一级？
→ 答案：B，盗窃（larceny）。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他先跟踪、还掏了枪，像是在准备 抢劫（robbery）。

但考试真正问的是：真正完成的是哪一个罪名，不是他脑子里曾经想过什么。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这里真正卡住抢劫的是：受害人已经昏倒，钱包又是直接从口袋拿走，命题人想骗你把“有枪”当成“有暴力抢劫”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 伸手进口袋拿走钱包 已完成 盗窃（larceny）；后来又把钱包丢掉，不会把已经完成的盗窃变成未遂。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 gun 当成自动成立抢劫，但这里没用暴力拿到财物。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间上诉理由误判

✕ C: 以为有未遂空间就行，但本题的财物其实已经拿走了。

❌ 事实误判 | 题干条件偷换

✕ D: 先偷到钱包再逃跑，不能倒推成 attempt。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清“已完成”还是“未完成”，再看有没有把抢劫抬高的暴力或恐吓。

考场速记

记住这条：盗窃（larceny） 看“拿走并带离”，抢劫（robbery） 额外要“人身/近旁 + 暴力或恐吓”。

这题一旦已经把钱包从口袋里取走，最高通常就是 盗窃（larceny）；后面临时放弃，只影响行动，不抹掉已完成的罪名。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
The CEO of a company, who spent many of her work hours surfing stamp-collector websites, frequently ordered expensive stamps that she had delivered to her work address. One day, a very rare and expensive stamp arrived in the mail. The CEO's assistant, who was resentful about the meager pay he received from the CEO, decided to steal the stamp. He checked the CEO's calendar and saw that she was attending the opera the following evening. The next night, after the CEO left for the opera, the assistant retrieved a spare key hidden under a rock and entered the CEO's home through the front door, which led straight into the living room where the stamp collection was prominently displayed. As the assistant searched through the stamp collection for the rare stamp, the front door suddenly opened and the CEO walked in. Upon seeing the assistant, the CEO reached into her purse, pulled out a gun, told the assistant to stay where he was, and called the police.
In a common-law jurisdiction, which of the following crime(s) can the assistant be found guilty of?

choices.A: No crime.
choices.B: Burglary only.
choices.C: Attempted larceny only.
choices.D: Burglary and attempted larceny.

questions.explanation:
Burglary

(failure to complete underlying felony)
specific intent
Assistant plans
to steal stamp
breaking & entering
Assistant enters
without consent
overt act
Assistant searches
for stamp
failure to complete
CEO catches
assistant

Common-law burglary requires proof that the defendant:

  • unlawfully broke and entered another's dwelling at night and
  • did so with the specific intent to commit a felony (e.g., larceny) therein.

An unlawful breaking occurs if the defendant used any amount of force to create an opening into the dwelling without consent. And once the defendant enters the dwelling with the requisite intent, the burglary is complete. This means that there is no need to prove that the defendant completed the underlying felony to obtain a burglary conviction.

In addition, a burglary defendant who fails to complete the underlying felony is also guilty of the attempted commission of that felony. That is because the defendant (1) specifically intended to commit the felony and (2) performed an overt act in furtherance of the felony—the unlawful breaking and entering. And the underlying felony (attempted or completed) does not merge with the burglary because neither offense requires all the elements of the other.

Here, since the assistant performed the overt act of unlawfully entering the CEO's home with the specific intent to commit larceny (i.e., to steal the stamp), he is guilty of attempted larceny (Choice B). And since the assistant unlawfully broke and entered the CEO's home at night with the specific intent to commit a felony (i.e., larceny), the assistant is also guilty of burglary (Choices A & C). Therefore, because these offenses will not merge, the assistant can be found guilty of both burglary and attempted larceny.

📌 Educational Objective

Common-law burglary is complete when the defendant unlawfully breaks and enters another's dwelling at night with the specific intent to commit a felony therein. If the underlying felony is not completed, then the defendant may be guilty of the attempted commission of that felony and burglary because the offenses do not merge.
questions.zh-question:
一家公司的CEO将她的大部分工作时间用于浏览集邮网站，并经常订购昂贵的邮票寄到她的工作地址。一天，一枚非常稀有且昂贵的邮票通过邮件送达。这位CEO的助理因对CEO付给他的微薄薪水心怀不满，决定偷走这枚邮票。他查看了CEO的日历，发现她第二天晚上要去听歌剧。第二天晚上，在CEO去听歌剧后，助理取回了藏在石头下的备用钥匙，从前门进入了CEO的家，前门直通客厅，那里显眼地陈列着邮票收藏品。正当助理在邮票收藏品中寻找那枚稀有邮票时，前门突然打开，CEO走了进来。看到助理后，CEO从她的钱包里掏出一把枪，告诉助理待在原地，然后报了警。

在普通法司法管辖区，该助理可能被裁定犯有以下哪项（或哪些）罪行？

zh-choices.A: 无罪。
zh-choices.B: 仅构成入室犯法罪。
zh-choices.C: 仅构成盗窃未遂罪。
zh-choices.D: 构成入室犯法罪和盗窃未遂罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Other Crimes

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：普通法 入室盗窃（burglary） 只看“非法破门进入 + 夜间 + 进入时有重罪意图”，不要求把里面想偷的东西真的偷到手；另外，没偷成还可能再加上 未遂盗窃（attempted larceny）。

三秒认题路径：

夜间入屋 → 未经同意 → 想偷财物 → 没偷成 → 双罪并存

核心法律规则

普通法 入室盗窃（burglary） 的核心是：在夜间非法 破门进入（breaking and entering） 他人住所，并且进入时就带着 特定故意（specific intent） 去实施重罪。考场意思：门一进、意图已在，盗窃还没得手也不影响 burglary 成立。

未遂犯罪（attempt） 需要两件事：想犯罪 + 做了向前推进的动作；这里的“进入并翻找”已经够作 overt act。考场意思：偷没偷到是另一条线，没完成就继续算 attempted larceny。

核心判例： 本题用的是普通法 burglary 规则，不需要完成基础重罪；进入时有盗窃意图就够了，所以可以同时成立 burglary 和 attempted larceny。

思维导图

先看 burglary：夜间、非法进入、进入时有偷窃意图？
事实1 助手先看日历，挑 CEO 不在家的夜晚下手。
事实2 他用藏好的备用钥匙从前门进屋，属于未经同意进入住所。
事实3 进屋时就想偷那枚稀有邮票，重罪意图已存在。
卡死点：burglary 不要求把邮票真的偷走。
再看 attempt：有没有想偷 + 已经迈出实施一步？
事实4 他进屋后直接翻找邮票，已经是向前推进的行为。
事实5 CEO 当场回来，偷窃没有完成。
卡死点：attempted larceny 成立；burglary 和 attempt 不合并。
结论：两个罪名都能扣上。
答案走向：Burglary and attempted larceny

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他最后没偷成，所以只有 attempt，或者 CEO 回来持枪阻止了他，案件就“没做完”。

但考试真正问的是：burglary 在进入那一刻就已经完成，后面有没有偷到只是另一条罪名的问题。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题别被“结果没得手”带跑：burglary 看进入时的意图，attempted larceny 看没完成偷窃。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里他先 未经同意进屋，而且进门时就想偷邮票，所以 burglary 已成；随后又翻找却没偷到，所以再成立 attempted larceny。

❌ 概念混淆 | 合并规则误判

✕ A: 把“没偷到”当成“没犯罪”，忽略了 burglary 早就完成。

❌ 法律适用 | 只看入口结果

✕ B: 只抓 burglary，漏掉后面的未遂盗窃。

❌ 事实误判 | 偷窃未完成偷换

✕ C: 以为只要没拿走邮票，attempt 就不存在。

这题建议用什么方法？

先盯“进入时有没有偷的心”，再单独看“偷没偷成”，不要把两步混成一个结论。

考场速记

记住一句：burglary 看“夜间非法进入 + 进门时有重罪意图”，attempted larceny 看“想偷 + 没偷成”。两个罪名通常可以同时成立，因为它们不要求完全相同的要件。

速记：entry + felonious intent = burglary；intent + overt act + failure = attempt。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Analyzing elements of burglary and attempted larceny

reason.en: Provides the specific intent to commit a felony required for burglary and attempt.
reason.zh: 提供了入室盗窃及未遂罪所要求的实施重罪的特定意图。

reason.en: Using an unauthorized key to open a door satisfies the breaking element of burglary.

reason.en: Incorrectly assumes the lack of a completed larceny or key usage negates all criminal liability.
reason.zh: 错误地认为未完成盗窃或使用钥匙免除了所有刑事责任。

label.zh: 仅构成入室盗窃干扰项

reason.en: Overlooks the substantial step taken towards larceny, which constitutes attempt.
reason.zh: 忽视了为实施盗窃所采取的实质性步骤，这构成了未遂。

label.zh: 仅构成盗窃未遂干扰项

reason.en: Fails to recognize that entry with an unauthorized key satisfies all burglary elements.
reason.zh: 未能认识到使用未经授权的钥匙进入满足了入室盗窃的所有要素。

reason.en: Correctly identifies that both burglary and attempted larceny are separate, fully established crimes.
reason.zh: 正确识别出入室盗窃和盗窃未遂是两个独立的、完全成立的罪行。

highlights.text: decided to steal the stamp

reason.en: Establishes the intent to commit a felony prior to entry, required for burglary.
reason.zh: 确立了进入前实施重罪的意图，这是入室盗窃所要求的。

highlights.text: retrieved a spare key hidden under a rock

reason.en: Unpermitted key usage serves as the breaking element in common-law burglary.
reason.zh: 未经许可使用钥匙可作为普通法入室盗窃罪中的强行侵入要素。

highlights.text: entered the CEO's home through the front door

reason.en: Satisfies the entry of a dwelling house element of burglary.
reason.zh: 满足了入室盗窃罪的侵入住宅要素。

highlights.text: searched through the stamp collection for the rare stamp

reason.en: Acts as the overt act beyond preparation required for attempted larceny.
reason.zh: 构成了盗窃未遂所要求的超越准备阶段的公开行为（实质性步骤）。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A woman was envious of her coworker for receiving a promotion they had both sought. After receiving the promotion, the coworker bought himself a very expensive watch to celebrate. The woman wanted to buy a similar watch, but she could not afford to do so. The coworker later invited the woman to attend a game night he was hosting, and the woman concocted a plan to steal the watch from him.
When the woman arrived at the coworker's house the following night, the coworker invited her in and showed her to the living room where they were playing games. Later in the evening, when no one was looking, the woman snuck into the coworker's bedroom, opened the bedroom closet, and rummaged through the closet until she found a display box in which the coworker kept his valuables. As anticipated, she found the watch inside the box, hid the watch in her jacket, and left with it at the end of the night.
The coworker reported the incident upon discovering that his watch was missing. The police interviewed all of the guests who attended the game night, and after seeing the woman wearing the watch in plain view, the police arrested the woman and charged her with burglary.
Is the woman guilty of burglary?

choices.A: No, because opening the coworker's watch box does not qualify as a breaking.
choices.B: No, because the woman had permission to enter all areas within the coworker's home.
choices.C: Yes, because the woman entered the coworker's home with the intent to steal the watch.
choices.D: Yes, because the woman opened the coworker's closet door with the intent to steal the watch.

questions.explanation:
Breaking requirement for burglary

When, as here, the question does not indicate that the majority rule is being tested, apply the common law rule for burglary. Common-law burglary is the:

  • unlawful breaking and entering of another's dwelling at nighttime
  • with the specific intent to commit a felony (eg, larceny) therein.

A breaking is accomplished when even slight force is used to create an opening into a dwelling—eg, opening an unlocked door or window. If the defendant instead entered the dwelling with consent, a breaking can still occur if the defendant later enters part of the dwelling structure (eg, opening a closet door or wall safe) without permission.

Here, the woman went to the coworker's house with the intent to steal his watch. But since the coworker invited the woman into his home for a game night, she did not break into his dwelling when she initially entered his home. However, she did break into the coworker's bedroom closet—part of the dwelling structure that she did not have permission to enter—later that evening. And since the woman entered the closet with the specific intent to steal the coworker's watch (ie, commit larceny), she is guilty of burglary (Choices B & C).*

*This fact pattern also meets the less-stringent majority and Model Penal Code standard for burglary, which merely requires the unlawful entry of a building or other structure with the specific intent to commit any crime therein.

(Choice A) Merely opening an object within a dwelling (eg, watch box, desk drawer, trunk) does not constitute a breaking because common law burglary seeks only to protect a person's right of habitation. However, the woman did commit burglary when she opened the bedroom closet with the requisite intent.

📌 Educational Objective

For burglary, a breaking can still occur after a defendant enters a dwelling with consent if the defendant subsequently enters part of the dwelling structure (eg, opening a closet door or wall safe) without consent. But merely opening an object within a dwelling (eg, desk drawer, trunk, box) is not a breaking.

📚 References
  • Charles E. Torcia, 3 Wharton's Criminal Law § 318 (15th ed. 2020) (stating that a breaking may occur within a dwelling by opening a closed inner door, such as a bedroom door, with the intent to commit a felony therein).
questions.zh-question:
一名女子因其同事获得了两人都曾追求的晋升而心生嫉妒。获得晋升后，该同事为自己买了一块非常昂贵的手表以示庆祝。该女子想买一块类似的手表，但她无力承担。之后，同事邀请该女子参加他举办的游戏之夜，该女子便策划了一个从他那里偷走手表的计划。

第二天晚上，当该女子到达同事家时，同事邀请她进屋，并带她到客厅玩游戏。当晚晚些时候，趁无人注意，该女子潜入同事的卧室，打开卧室壁橱，在壁橱里翻找，直到找到了一个同事存放贵重物品的展示盒。正如所料，她在盒子里找到了那块手表，将手表藏在夹克里，并在当晚结束时带着它离开。

同事发现手表丢失后报了警。警方询问了所有参加游戏之夜的客人，在看到该女子公然佩戴着那块手表后，警方逮捕了该女子，并以入室犯法罪（burglary）起诉她。

该女子是否犯有入室犯法罪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为打开同事的手表盒不构成“破门而入”（breaking）。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该女子已获得许可进入同事家中的所有区域。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为该女子进入同事家时意图窃取手表。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该女子打开同事的壁橱门时意图窃取手表。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：普通法 burglary 里，“breaking”不只看进门那一下，还看你后面有没有未经许可进入屋内的结构部分，比如打开卧室衣柜。

三秒认题路径：

先看是否同意进入 → 再看屋内结构 → 重点是 closet → 有无盗窃意图 → 选 burglary

核心法律规则

普通法 burglary 的考场意思：unlawful breaking and entering 他人住宅，并且在进入时就有偷窃等重罪意图。

breaking 的考场意思：轻微用力制造进入通道就算，哪怕是一扇门、一扇窗，甚至屋内某个你本来没权进入的结构部分，也可能算。

所以这题的关键不是她最开始能不能进屋，而是她后来有没有未经许可打开卧室衣柜；有，就把 breaking 补齐了。

核心判例：Wharton’s Criminal Law 所述规则锁定：打开卧室门、衣柜门、墙保险箱这类“屋内结构”时，若伴随盗窃意图，也能构成 burglary。

思维导图

1. 她一开始进屋时，算不算 burglary 的 breaking？
否 邀请入内，所以第一次进门不是“闯入”。
2. 那后来呢？她有没有再进入屋内的结构部分？
是 她未经许可打开卧室衣柜，衣柜门属于屋内结构。
卡死点：不是打开 watch box；真正致命的是打开 closet door。
3. 打开衣柜时，她脑子里在想什么？
有 她当时就是为了找并偷走手表，满足进入时的盗窃意图。
结论：这次“屋内再闯入” + 盗窃意图 = burglary。
对应答案 选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她只是打开了 watch box，好像只是拿盒子里的东西，不像“破门而入”。

但考试真正问的是：她有没有打开自己本来无权进入的屋内结构；这里真正触发的是 closet door，不是小盒子。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的 opened the bedroom closet 正好是对屋内结构的未经许可进入；她当时又是为偷表而去，所以满足 burglary 的 breaking + 盗窃意图。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 watch box 当成 breaking 了，命题人骗你忽略真正的 closet。

❌ 事实误判 | 许可范围偷换

✕ B: 她只被请进客厅，不是被授权随便进所有房间。

❌ 法律适用 | 进门节点误判

✕ C: 只盯着最初进屋，忽略后面未经许可的屋内再进入。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“同意进入”与“屋内结构”两层，再看目的是否在进入时就已存在。

考场速记

记住一句：进入房子不等于没 burglary，只要后来又未经许可打开屋内结构，并且当时带着偷窃意图，照样能成立。

口诀：breaking can happen inside，closet door 可以，watch box 不行。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Determine burglary breaking of inner structures

reason.en: Negates a breaking at the initial entry of the dwelling.
reason.zh: 否定了最初进入住宅时的折入要素。

reason.en: Serves as the breaking of an inner part of the dwelling structure.
reason.zh: 构成对住宅内部结构（壁橱门）的折入行为。

reason.en: Establishes the specific intent required for burglary.
reason.zh: 确立了成立入室盗窃罪所需的特定意图。

reason.en: Opening a container is not a breaking of the dwelling structure.
reason.zh: 开启容器不属于对住宅结构的折入行为。

reason.en: Correctly states that opening a box isn't a breaking, but ignores the closet door.
reason.zh: 正确说明开启箱子不构成折入，但忽略了壁橱门。

reason.en: Misrepresents the scope of consent given to a guest.
reason.zh: 错误歪曲了给予访客的允许范围。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
An employee and her boss were leaving work late one evening. As they were passing a dark alleyway on the way to their cars, the defendant jumped out holding a knife. The defendant abruptly pushed the boss against the wall of a nearby building, held the knife to the boss's throat, and demanded the watch on his wrist. The boss complied. The defendant then turned to the employee and threatened to stab the boss if the employee did not hand over her money. The employee handed her wallet to the defendant, who took the wallet and ran away. Shortly thereafter, the police found and arrested the defendant.
What crime(s) can the defendant be properly convicted of?

choices.A: Assault on the employee, battery on the boss, and robbery from both the employee and the boss.
choices.B: Battery on the boss, and larceny from both the employee and the boss.
choices.C: Larceny from the employee and the boss, and robbery from the boss.
choices.D: Robbery from both the employee and the boss.

questions.explanation:
Robbery (greater offense)
Larceny (lesser offense)
  • Unlawful taking & carrying away of victim's property
  • Specific intent to permanently deprive
+
Battery (lesser offense)
  • force used to cause bodily injury or offensive touching
OR
Assault (lesser offense)
  • attempted battery or conduct causing apprehension of imminent harm

Larceny is the unlawful taking and carrying away of the victim's personal property with the specific intent to permanently deprive the victim of that property (ie, to steal). Larceny is elevated to robbery when:

  • the property is taken from the victim's person or presence and
  • the taking is achieved by force or threat of force against the victim, the victim's family member, or another person present.

The threat-of-force element of robbery can be satisfied by a battery, which is the unlawful application of force to another resulting in bodily injury or an offensive touching. This element can also be satisfied by an assault, which is an attempted battery or conduct that intentionally puts the victim in reasonable apprehension of imminent bodily harm.

Here, the defendant battered the boss by grabbing him, pushing him against a wall, and holding a knife to his throat. The defendant also assaulted the boss by threatening to stab him. But the defendant did not assault the employee since he did not attempt to batter her or place her in apprehension of bodily harm (Choice A). The defendant then committed larceny by taking the boss's watch and the employee's wallet.

Both larcenies elevated to robbery since (1) the taking from the boss was accomplished by force and threat of force against him and (2) the taking from the employee was achieved by threatening force against the boss. Since larceny satisfies the taking requirement for robbery—and both battery and assault satisfy the threat-of-force requirement—all three crimes are lesser included offenses. This means that they merge with the robbery and the defendant can only be convicted of robbery; not the other crimes (Choices B & C).

📌 Educational Objective

Robbery requires a taking of the victim's property by force or intimidation. Since larceny satisfies the taking requirement and battery/assault satisfy the force or intimidation requirement, they are lesser included offenses that merge with robbery.
questions.zh-question:
一天深夜，一名女雇员和她的老板正要下班离开。当他们路过一条通往停车场的黑暗小巷时，被告人持刀跳了出来。被告人突然将老板推到附近一栋建筑的墙上，用刀抵住老板的喉咙，并索要他手腕上的手表。老板照做了。随后，被告人转向女雇员，并威胁说如果女雇员不交出她的钱，他就会刺伤老板。女雇员将钱包交给了被告人，被告人拿走钱包后逃跑了。不久之后，警方找到并逮捕了被告人。

被告人可以被正式定罪的罪行是？

zh-choices.A: 对女雇员构成攻击罪(Assault)，对老板构成伤害罪(battery)，以及对女雇员和老板均构成抢劫罪(robbery)。
zh-choices.B: 对老板构成伤害罪(battery)，以及对女雇员和老板均构成盗窃罪(larceny)。
zh-choices.C: 对女雇员和老板均构成盗窃罪(larceny)，以及对老板构成抢劫罪(robbery)。
zh-choices.D: 对女雇员和老板均构成抢劫罪(robbery)。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：抢劫（robbery）是否成立，以及同一串事实里被害人财物被夺时，盗窃（larceny）、殴打（battery）、袭击（assault）为什么都要并入抢劫，不单独再判。

三秒认题路径：

先看拿走财物 → 再看有无暴力/威吓 → 再判抢劫 → 最后看轻罪并入

核心法律规则

盗窃（larceny）是把别人的动产拿走并带走，还要有永久剥夺的故意；考试意思：先有“偷”。

如果财物是从被害人本人或其在场范围内拿走，而且是靠暴力（force）或威吓（intimidation）完成，盗窃就升级成抢劫（robbery）；考试意思：同样是偷，但这次“动手了”。

殴打（battery）和袭击（assault）都能充当抢劫里的暴力/威吓要素，所以它们通常和抢劫并为轻罪，最后不单独再判。

核心判例： 本题不靠单一判例定胜负，关键是普通法抢劫规则：larceny + force/threat = robbery，轻罪并入抢劫。

思维导图

先问：有没有把财物从被害人本人或在场范围内拿走？
有 先构成盗窃（larceny）的“拿走”要素。
再问：取财时有没有对被害人用刀、推搡、威胁或让其害怕？
有 触发抢劫（robbery）；这里的battery/assault只是抢劫的暴力工具。
卡死点：一旦抢劫成立，larceny、battery、assault都作为轻罪并入，不能再单独重判。
最后落点：两个被害人的财物都被拿走了吗？
有 对老板是持刀逼抢；对员工是拿老板做人质式威胁后夺钱包，所以两笔都算抢劫。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：先挥刀、再逼人交出钱包，好像应该先拆成battery、assault、larceny分别定罪。

但考试真正问的是：这串行为是不是已经被robbery一网打尽，前面的轻罪会不会并入。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

老板被刀逼着交表，员工被“威胁拿老板开刀”逼着交钱包，这种题最爱骗你把事实拆太细；真正要抓的是“取财 + 暴力/威吓”这条线。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里老板那笔是持刀逼迫交表，员工那笔是拿老板作威胁逼交钱包；两笔都满足抢劫，所以只能判两项抢劫。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把员工那段误看成独立assault，其实她只是被威胁后交钱。

❌ 事实误判 | 题干条件偷换

✕ B: 只看到“拿走”就想成larceny，漏掉了当场持刀和威胁。

❌ 法律适用 | 轻罪并入误判

✕ C: 以为老板那笔只能算robbery，员工那笔还可单列盗窃，忽略两笔都已升级。

这题建议用什么方法？

先把“拿走”与“暴力/威吓”合并看，再统一判断轻罪是否并入抢劫。

考场速记

记住一句：larceny + force/threat = robbery；一旦抢劫成立，battery 和 assault通常不再单独罚。

这类题先找“谁的财物、怎么拿、有没有刀和威胁”，别被剧情带跑。

B.text: larceny from both the employee and the boss

reason.en: Threatening a person present (the boss) to coerce another (the employee) elevates the larceny from the employee to robbery.
reason.zh: 通过威胁在场人员（老板）来强迫另一人（雇员）交付财物，将针对雇员的盗窃行为升格为抢劫罪。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Unprepared for a final examination, a student asked his girlfriend to set off the fire alarms in the university building 15 minutes after the test commenced. The girlfriend did so. Several students were injured in the panic that followed as people were trying to get out of the building.
If both the student and the girlfriend are prosecuted for battery and for conspiracy to commit battery, what is the likely result?

choices.A: They are guilty of both crimes.
choices.B: They are guilty of battery but not conspiracy.
choices.C: They are guilty of conspiracy but not battery.
choices.D: They are not guilty of either crime.

questions.explanation:
Types of mens rea

Battery is the unlawful application of force to another person that results in bodily harm to that person or constitutes an offensive touching. Battery is a general intent crime, so the contact need not be intentionally inflicted. Criminal negligence—i.e., a gross deviation from the level of care a reasonable person would use under similar circumstances—is enough to support a battery conviction. And the force can be directly or indirectly applied by a third party acting under the defendant's direction or by an object controlled by the defendant.

Here, several students were injured when the fire alarms caused people to exit the building in a panic. Although the girlfriend did not intend to inflict harm or cause offense when she set off the alarms, she was criminally negligent when she did so during an exam. And the force was indirectly applied by the people rushing out of the school in panic. Therefore, she is guilty of battery. And since the student acted as her accomplice when he encouraged her to set off the alarms, he is liable to the same extent as the girlfriend (Choices C & D).

Conspiracy requires proof that (1) the defendant entered an agreement with the specific intent to commit a crime and (2) an overt act was committed in furtherance of that agreement. Here, the student and the girlfriend agreed that she would pull the fire alarms. But since they did not enter that agreement with the specific intent to commit battery, they are not guilty of conspiracy to commit battery (Choices A & C).

📌 Educational Objective

General intent crimes (e.g., battery) require at least criminally negligent conduct—i.e., grossly deviating from the level of care a reasonable person would use under similar circumstances. But specific intent crimes (e.g., conspiracy) require intentional conduct—i.e., purposefully or knowingly causing a particular result.
questions.zh-question:
一个学生因期末考试未准备好，让其女友在考试开始15分钟后，在教学楼内拉响火警警报。其女友照做了。在随后人们惊慌逃离大楼的过程中，有几名学生受伤。

如果该学生和其女友均被以伤害罪（battery）和共谋伤害罪（conspiracy to commit battery）起诉，最可能的结果是什么？

zh-choices.A: 他们两项罪名都成立。
zh-choices.B: 他们伤害罪罪名成立，但共谋罪罪名不成立。
zh-choices.C: 他们共谋罪罪名成立，但伤害罪罪名不成立。
zh-choices.D: 他们两项罪名都不成立。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes Against the Person

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：battery（殴打罪） 属于general intent（一般故意），即使不是直接动手，只要引发了造成伤害的间接力量，也可能成立；但conspiracy（共谋）要的是对犯罪结果的specific intent（特定故意），只想恶作剧不够。

三秒认题路径：

间接致伤 → 殴打罪 → 一般故意 → 只恶作剧不够共谋 → 选 B

核心法律规则

battery（殴打罪） 的考场意思：对他人实施非法用力，造成身体伤害或令人厌恶的接触；它是general intent（一般故意）罪，所以不要求行为人一定“就是想打伤人”。

criminal negligence（刑事过失） 的考场意思：只要偏离合理人的注意义务到很夸张，题目就可能把你推到 battery 里。这里报警器在考试中间被拉响，学生慌乱冲出导致受伤，force（力量） 是通过人群惊慌这种间接方式发生的，仍可算 battery。

conspiracy（共谋） 的考场意思：要先有为了犯罪而达成的协议，还要有完成协议的外在行为；如果双方只是想捣乱、拖考试，不是为了 battery，就缺少共谋所需的特定故意。

核心判例： 本题考的是常规 MBE 规则，不靠额外判例；抓住“battery 可由刑事过失 + 间接力量成立，但 conspiracy 需要针对 battery 的特定故意”就够了。

思维导图

先看伤害是怎么来的：报警器引发人群惊慌，伤害是“间接”出来的。
关卡 1：这算不算 battery（殴打罪）？
直接卡死点：general intent 不要求真想伤人；criminal negligence 已够。
结果：女孩拉警报时虽未想伤人，但在考试时制造惊慌，仍可成立 battery。
关卡 2：这算不算 conspiracy（共谋）？
先要协议 + 外在行为没错，但还得有“为了 battery 的特定故意”。
这里他们只同意“拉警报”，不是同意“实施 battery” → 共谋不成立。
结论：女孩 guilty of battery；两人都不 guilty of conspiracy → 选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她没打人、也没故意伤人，所以 battery 应该不成立。

但考试真正问的是：battery（殴打罪） 不只看“有没有亲手打”，还看有没有通过间接力量造成伤害；而 conspiracy（共谋） 不是“大家一起干了点坏事”就算，得是为了那个犯罪结果而合意。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 考试中拉响警报导致学生慌乱受伤，足够支持 battery；但两人只是想让考试受干扰，不是为了 battery，所以不成 conspiracy。

❌ 概念混淆 | 一起作恶误判

✕ A: 把“有合意”误当成“有针对 battery 的合意”。

❌ 法律适用 | 特定故意错位

✕ C: 只盯着 specific intent，却漏掉 battery 还能由间接伤害成立。

❌ 事实误判 | 伤害来源偷换

✕ D: 把人群冲撞造成的伤害当成“没人动手”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清一般故意和特定故意，再问伤害是不是可以由间接力量推到 battery。

考场速记

记忆口诀：battery 看结果和间接力量，conspiracy 看协议是否瞄准犯罪结果。这题就记成：“能伤到人”≠“想伤到人”；“一起做坏事”≠“一起合谋这个罪”。

B.text: guilty of battery but not conspiracy

reason.en: Correctly applies criminal negligence for battery and the lack of specific intent for conspiracy.

reason.zh: 未能认识到刑事疏忽足以构成殴击罪且适用共犯责任。

highlights.text: asked his girlfriend to set off the fire alarms

reason.en: Shows they agreed to set off alarms but did not agree to commit battery (no intent to injure).
reason.zh: 表明他们同意拉响警报，但并未同意实施殴击罪（无伤害意图）。

reason.en: Satisfies the physical harm element of battery caused by criminal negligence.
reason.zh: 满足由刑事疏忽引起殴击罪的身体伤害要素。

highlights.text: prosecuted for battery and for conspiracy to commit battery

reason.en: Triggers the need to analyze general intent vs. specific intent requirements.
reason.zh: 触发需要分析普通意图与特定意图要求的分析。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A state statute makes it a crime to "knowingly possess a controlled substance analogue." The statute defines a "controlled substance analogue" (CSA) as a substance that has a chemical structure similar to a controlled substance and has a physiological effect on humans similar to or greater than a controlled substance. A defendant was arrested for possession of a synthetic stimulant known by its street name as "bath salts" and was charged with violating the criminal statute.
Regarding the knowledge element of this crime as it relates to the substance found in the defendant's possession, which of the following is the most proper jury instruction?

choices.A: "If you find that the defendant knew that the substance he possessed was an illegal CSA, you must find the defendant guilty."
choices.B: "If you find that the defendant knew that the substance he possessed was illegal or had a chemical structure similar to a controlled substance and physiological effects on humans similar to or greater than a controlled substance, you must find the defendant guilty."
choices.C: "If you find that the defendant possessed a substance that was a CSA, you must find the defendant guilty even if the defendant did not know that the substance was a CSA or illegal."
choices.D: "If you find that the substance possessed by the defendant is commonly known to have a chemical structure similar to a controlled substance and physiological effects on humans similar to or greater than a controlled substance, you must find the defendant guilty."

questions.explanation:
Possession of controlled substance
(dual-knowledge requirement)
Knowledge of possession Defendant must knowingly possess substance—ie:
  • exercise dominion & control over substance
Knowledge of item Defendant must know that substance is controlled—ie:
  • know that substance is prohibited by law, even if defendant does not know specific identity of substance or
  • know facts about substance that make possession illegal, even if defendant does not know possession is illegal

When a statute makes it a crime to knowingly possess an item, the word "knowingly" applies to the statute's verb (possess) as well as the object of that verb (controlled substance analogue (CSA)). As a result, a conviction under this statute requires proof that the defendant knowingly possessed the substance and either:

  • knew that the substance was prohibited by law—even if the defendant did not know the specific identity of the substance—or
  • knew facts about the substance that made possessing it illegal—eg, knew that it had a chemical structure similar to a controlled substance and physiological effects on humans similar to or greater than a controlled substance—even if the defendant did not know that possessing it was illegal.

A jury instruction regarding the knowledge element of this crime as it relates to the substance found in the defendant's possession must include both of the above bullet points (Choice A).

The jury instruction should therefore read: "If you find that the defendant knew that the substance he possessed was illegal (prohibited by law) or had a chemical structure similar to a controlled substance and physiological effects on humans similar to or greater than a controlled substance (facts making its possession illegal), you must find the defendant guilty."

(Choices C & D) Mere possession of a substance later identified as a controlled substance or an analogue thereof is not sufficient to convict the defendant. Nor is it sufficient that the substance possessed by the defendant is commonly known (by the public at large) as a CSA. Instead, the defendant must have known that the substance is illegal or known facts about the substance that made possessing it illegal.

📌 Educational Objective

In prosecutions for possession of a controlled substance or analogue thereof, the defendant's knowledge that the substance was a controlled substance or analogue may be established by evidence that the defendant knew (1) the substance was prohibited by law or (2) facts about the substance that made possessing it illegal.

📚 References
  • McFadden v. United States, 576 U.S. 186, 194–96 (2015) (applying the dual-knowledge requirement to controlled substance analogue prosecutions).
questions.zh-question:
一部州法律规定“明知而持有管控物质类似物”构成犯罪。该法律将“管控物质类似物”（CSA）定义为一种化学结构与管控物质相似，且对人体产生的生理效应与管控物质相似或更强的物质。一名被告因持有一种俗称为“bath salts”的合成兴奋剂而被捕，并被控违反该刑事法规。

关于本罪中与被告持有的物质相关的明知要素，以下哪项是为最适当的陪审团指令？

zh-choices.A: “如果你们认定被告明知其所持有的物质为一种非法的CSA，你们必须裁定被告有罪。”
zh-choices.B: “如果你们认定被告明知其持有的物质是非法的，或者明知该物质具有与管控物质相似的化学结构、以及对人体具有与管控物质相似或更强的生理效应，你们必须裁定被告有罪。”
zh-choices.C: “如果你们认定被告持有的物质是一种CSA，你们必须裁定被告有罪，即使被告并不知道该物质是一种CSA或属非法。”
zh-choices.D: “如果你们认定，被告所持有的物质，是众所周知具有与管控物质相似的化学结构、以及对人体具有与管控物质相似或更强的生理效应的物质，你们必须裁定被告有罪。”

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Other Crimes

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：持有受控物质类似物（controlled substance analogue） 的 知情要件（knowledge element） 要不要同时知道“自己在持有”以及“该物质违法或具备违法特征”。

三秒认题路径：

先看 knowingly → 再看对象 → 双重知情 → 选含两层 → 排除“只要持有”

核心法律规则

这类题考的是 knowingly（明知） 同时修饰“持有”动作和“所持物质”的性质，考场意思：不是只要你拿着东西就算数，还要你知道自己在拿什么。对 受控物质类似物（controlled substance analogue, CSA），检方要证明被告要么知道它受法律禁止（prohibited by law），要么知道让它违法的事实，比如它的化学结构和生理作用都像受控物质。只知道“手里有个后来被认出来的东西”不够。

核心判例： McFadden v. United States — 确认 CSA 案件适用“双重知情”标准。

思维导图

题目先问：被告只“持有”了吗？
第一层：要先有 knowingly possess，即明知地占有并控制该物质。
第二层：再看他知不知道对象是 CSA，路径二选一：
A 知道它违法（illegal）；
B 知道让它违法的事实：化学结构像受控物质、药效也像或更强。
卡死点：只知道“后来被查出是 bath salts”不够；不知道违法性或违法事实，就过不了知情门槛。
结论：题干要找的是“双重知情”的完整指令，故选能同时覆盖两种认知路径的选项。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然被告拿的是 bath salts，而且它最后被认定是 CSA，那就直接推定有罪。

但考试真正问的是：被告当时知不知道它违法，或者知不知道让它违法的那些事实，而不是事后才知道它是什么。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干问的是 knowledge element，B 同时抓住“知道违法”或“知道违法事实”两条路，正好对应 双重知情（dual-knowledge）。

❌ 概念混淆 | 只看违法标签

✕ A: 把“知道是非法”偷换成“知道就必然有罪”，少了对持有和对象认知的完整表述。

❌ 法律适用 | 只凭事后认定

✕ C: 只靠 possessed a substance 就定罪，直接跳过知情要件。

❌ 事实误判 | 公共常识代替明知

✕ D: 把“大家都知道”当成被告知道，题目要的是被告自己的认知，不是街头名称。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定 knowingly 修饰范围，再检查被告是否知道“违法”或知道“违法事实”。

考场速记

记住这句：knowingly 不是只管“拿没拿”，还管“知不知道它为什么违法”。遇到 CSA 题，就背“双重知情”：知道违法，或知道让它违法的事实。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A woman told a man to accompany her into her friend's unlocked barn and retrieve an expensive black saddle that she said she had loaned to the friend. The man accompanied the woman to the friend's barn, opened the door, found a black saddle hanging high above the ground, and climbed a ladder to reach it. He handed the saddle down to the woman, and the two left with it together. In fact, the saddle belonged to the friend, and when the friend discovered the saddle missing, she suspected that the woman was the thief. The friend used a screwdriver to break into the woman's house to find the saddle. Upon discovering the saddle on the woman's kitchen table, the friend took it back and called the police.
The jurisdiction follows the common law, except that burglary covers structures in addition to dwellings and the nighttime element has been eliminated.
Which of these individuals is guilty of burglary?

choices.A: All of them.
choices.B: Only the friend.
choices.C: Only the woman.
choices.D: The man and the woman.

questions.explanation:
In this jurisdiction, burglary is:

  • the unlawful breaking and entering of another's structure or dwelling—eg, use of slight force to open a door and step through the doorway
  • with the specific intent to commit a felony therein.

Larceny is a felony that occurs when a person unlawfully takes and carries away another's personal property with the specific intent to permanently deprive the owner of it. And a person is guilty of these crimes if he/she personally committed the crime OR used an innocent agent to commit the criminal acts. An innocent agent is a person who lacked the requisite mens rea but was tricked or forced into committing the crime.

Here, the man was an innocent agent of the woman since she falsely told him that she had loaned the saddle to the friend to trick the man into helping her take it from the friend's barn. The woman then used the man to open the unlocked barn door (unlawful breaking) and they entered the barn. Since the woman entered intending to steal the friend's saddle (larceny), she is guilty of burglary. But since the man believed that the woman owned the saddle (no intent to commit larceny or other felony), he is not guilty of burglary (Choices A & D).

The friend then discovered that her saddle was missing. She immediately suspected that the woman stole it, so the friend broke and entered the woman's house to retrieve it. But the friend did not intend to steal another's property because she owned the saddle. And since she did not intend to commit larceny or any other felony, the friend is not guilty of burglary (Choices A & B).

📌 Educational Objective

A person is guilty if he/she personally commits a crime or uses an innocent agent to commit the criminal acts. An innocent agent is a person who lacked the requisite mens rea but was tricked or forced into committing the crime.

该司法管辖区遵循普通法，但入室犯法罪的范围除了住宅外还包括其他建筑物，且夜间犯罪的要素已被废除。

这些人中，谁犯有入室犯法罪？

zh-choices.A: 他们全部都有罪。
zh-choices.B: 只有朋友有罪。
zh-choices.C: 只有女子有罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：入室盗窃（burglary）里，能不能把一个无辜代理人（innocent agent）当作自己的手来完成“破门而入 + 盗取财物”的犯罪动作。

三秒认题路径：

破门进入 → 有偷心 → 借人代手 → 代理人无犯意 → 只有女人有罪

核心法律规则

入室盗窃（burglary）的核心是：非法破门（breaking）并进入他人结构物（structure），而且进入时要带着实施重罪的特定故意（specific intent to commit a felony）。考场意思：不是“进去了”就够，关键是进去那一刻心里要想偷或想犯重罪。

如果当事人自己没有亲手完成动作，但他利用无辜代理人（innocent agent）去做，就等于自己亲手做了。考场意思：代理人只是被你骗着搬东西、开门、拿物，你的犯意会直接算到你头上。

核心判例： 无需记具体案名；本题按常见 MBE 规则，innocent agent 会把行为归到幕后操控者身上。

思维导图

先看谁“自己带着犯意”进了 barn？
否：男人只以为是在帮拿自家 saddle，没有偷窃故意，所以不能把 burglary 算到他头上。
是：女人让他去开门、拿 saddle，自己心里想的是把朋友的 saddle 偷走。
卡死点：她借男人“开门进 barn”的动作完成破门进入，且进入时已有偷窃意图。
再问 friend 进 woman house 时呢？
否：她只是去拿回自己的 saddle，不是去偷别人的东西；没有实施 felony 的特定故意，所以不构成 burglary。
最后结论
答案：只有女人有 burglary；男人是无辜代理人，friend 只是取回自有财物。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：friend 也是breaking and entering，是不是也算 burglary。

但考试真正问的是：进去时有没有偷别人财物的特定故意；friend 只是去拿回自己的 saddle，不是去偷别人的东西。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。本题换成 burglary 也是同样思路：看的是进入时的犯意，不是外表动作像不像偷。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

女人让男人替自己开门进 barn，再一起把朋友的 saddle 带走，男人只是无辜代理人；女人进入时已有偷窃意图，所以只有她构成 burglary。

❌ 概念混淆 | 代理归责误判

✕ A: 把所有“进门拿东西”的人都算成 burglary，漏掉了谁有偷心、谁只是被骗着帮忙。

❌ 事实误判 | 取回自物误判

✕ B: 以为 friend 破门进屋就一定是偷，其实她是在拿回自己的 saddle，没有盗取他人财物的意思。

❌ 法律适用 | 双人同罪误判

✕ D: 以为两个人一起搬走 saddle 就都成立，忽略了男人不知情、没有 burglary 所需犯意。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“谁有特定故意”，再看有没有借无辜代理人（innocent agent）完成破门进入。

考场速记

记住一句：burglary 不是看“谁碰了门”，而是看“谁带着偷的心进了门”。innocent agent 只会帮幕后那个人背动作，不会替自己长出犯意。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question: In which of the following cases is a defendant most likely to be convicted if charged with receiving stolen property?

choices.A: The defendant bought a car from a man. Before the purchase, the man told the defendant that the car was stolen. The man had stolen the car with the help of a friend who, unknown to the defendant or the man, was an undercover police informant who feigned cooperation with the man in the theft of the car.
choices.B: The defendant bought a car from a man. Before the purchase, the man told the defendant that the car was stolen. Unknown to the defendant, the man had stolen the car from a parking lot and had been caught by the police as he was driving it away. The man agreed to cooperate with the police and carry through with his prearranged sale of the car to the defendant.
choices.C: The defendant bought a car from a man. Before the purchase, the man told the defendant that the car was stolen. Unknown to the defendant, the man was in fact the owner of the car but had reported it to the police as stolen and had collected on a fraudulent claim of its theft from his insurance company.
choices.D: The defendant bought a car from a man who operates a used car lot. Before the purchase, the man told the defendant that the car had been stolen, which was true. Unknown to the defendant, the man is an undercover police informant who is operating the lot in cooperation with the police in exchange for leniency in connection with criminal charges pending against him.

A defendant is guilty of receiving stolen property if he/she:

  • took possession of, or exercised control over, stolen personal property
  • knew that the property was stolen and
  • specifically intended to permanently deprive the owner of the property.

But property is no longer considered stolen once the police recover the property—ie, locate and exercise control over it.

Here, the defendant bought a car from the man after the man told the defendant that it was stolen (knowledge and intent). The man stole the car with a friend who, unbeknownst to the man and the defendant, had been working as an undercover police informant. But since the police did not recover the stolen car before the defendant's purchase (possession), the defendant will likely be convicted of receiving stolen property.

(Choice B) The defendant bought a car from the man after being told that it was stolen. Although the man had taken the car from a parking lot, he was stopped and the car was recovered by police before the defendant took possession. Therefore, the car is not considered stolen and the defendant would likely be acquitted.

(Choice C) Although the defendant intended to buy a stolen car from the man, the man actually owned it. Therefore, the car was not stolen property.

(Choice D) The defendant bought a car from the man after being told that it had been stolen. But since the man operated the used car lot in cooperation with the police, the police exercised control over the car before the defendant took possession. Therefore, the car is considered recovered—not stolen.

📌 Educational Objective

Receiving stolen property requires proof that the defendant (1) took possession of, or exercised control over, stolen personal property, (2) knew that the property was stolen, and (3) specifically intended to permanently deprive the owner of it. But once stolen property is recovered by police, it is no longer considered stolen.

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：受领赃物（receiving stolen property）里，车在你买到前有没有先被警察“收回”成 not stolen。

三秒认题路径：

先看车是否赃物 → 再看警察有无收回 → 再看你是否拿到 → 还能定罪才选对

核心法律规则

受领赃物（receiving stolen property）要看三件事：你有没有取得赃物的占有或控制，明知是赃物（knowledge that property was stolen），以及想永久剥夺原主。

但只要警察已经把车找回并实际控制，物就不再算 赃物（stolen property） 了。考试上这句话很关键：你后来再买到的，只是“看起来像赃物”，不一定还能构成本罪。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用；本题的锁定规则是“被警方收回后，物不再是赃物”，所以关键不在你有没有听到“stolen”，而在买之前警察有没有先控制它。

思维导图

先问：这辆车在被告买入前，还是不是 赃物（stolen property）？
是车没被警察找回 → 仍算赃物 → 再看被告是否知道且买入占有 → 可成立受领赃物 → 对应正确选项
否警察已先收回 / 实际控制 → 物已变成 not stolen → 第三要件卡死 → 不能定罪
本题钉子选项里真正能过关的是：偷车时有卧底配合，但警察没有在被告购买前先收回那辆车。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然被告明知“这是偷来的车”，那应该都能定罪。

但考试真正问的是：车在被告拿到时还是不是赃物，不是你主观上有多坏。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。在这题里，真正致命的是警察有没有先把车收回。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干先告诉被告车是偷来的，而且警察并没有在他买车前先把车收回，所以买入时车仍是 stolen property，三要件才可能成立。

❌ 事实误判 | 漏看收回时间

✕ B: 漏掉 recovered by police，所以物已不再是赃物。

❌ 概念混淆 | 真假赃物混同

✕ C: 把“听起来像偷车”当成真赃物，但车主根本没失去所有权。

❌ 法律适用 | 卧底控制误套

✕ D: 看到 working with police 就以为还能算赃物，其实警方已先控制。

这题建议用什么方法？

先卡“买时还是不是赃物”，再看知识和占有，最后才判断能不能定罪。

考场速记

记忆口诀：先被警察收回，就不再是赃物。买家就算知道来源可疑，也要先过“物还算不算 stolen”的门槛。
