questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A customer asked to see an expensive watch in a jewelry store. In conversation with the store clerk, the customer falsely claimed to be the son of the mayor. When handed the watch, the customer asked if he could put it on, walk around a bit so he could see how it felt on his wrist, and briefly step outside to observe it in natural light. The clerk agreed, saying, "I know I can trust someone like you with the merchandise." The customer walked out of the store wearing the watch and did not return. A week later, the clerk was at a gathering when she spotted the customer wearing the watch. She told him that he must either pay for the watch or give it back. He hissed, "You'll be sorry if you mess with me." Intimidated, the clerk backed off.
The following list of crimes is in descending order of seriousness.
What is the most serious crime the customer committed?

choices.A: Robbery.
choices.B: Larceny.
choices.C: False pretenses.
choices.D: Embezzlement.

questions.explanation:
Distinguishing property crimes

Larceny
  • Unlawful taking & carrying away of another's property
  • With specific intent to steal
By a known misrepresentation
  • From victim's person/presence
  • By force or intimidation
Obtaining possession
Obtaining title
Larceny by trick
False pretenses
Robbery

Larceny occurs when a person (1) unlawfully takes and carries away another's personal property (2) with the specific intent to permanently deprive the owner of that property. An unlawful taking occurs when a person obtains possession of another's property without privilege or valid consent. This can arise when consent is obtained by knowingly misrepresenting a past or present material fact (ie, larceny by trick).

Here, the customer took the watch and carried it outside with the intent to permanently keep it. And though the clerk gave the customer permission to take the watch, she only did so because the customer falsely told her that he was the mayor's son. As a result, the clerk's consent was invalid, and the customer committed larceny.

(Choice A) Larceny is elevated to robbery when property is taken from another by force or intimidation. Here, the customer merely used deception to take the watch. And though he later intimidated the clerk with his threat, the unlawful taking and carrying away had already occurred. Therefore, no robbery occurred.

(Choice C) The crime of false pretenses differs from larceny by trick in that the defendant acquires title to—not just custody or possession of—the property. Since the customer merely obtained custody of the watch, he did not commit false pretenses.

(Choice D) Embezzlement is the fraudulent conversion of another's property by a person in lawful possession of that property. Here, no embezzlement occurred because the customer unlawfully possessed the watch due to his misrepresentation.

📌 Educational Objective

Larceny is (1) the unlawful taking and carrying away of another's personal property with (2) the specific intent to permanently deprive the owner of it. A taking is unlawful when the person obtains possession of property without the owner's valid consent—eg, by knowingly misrepresenting a past or present material fact.
questions.zh-question:
一名顾客在一家珠宝店要求看一块昂贵的手表。在与店员交谈时，该顾客谎称自己是市长的儿子。当手表递给他时，该顾客问他是否可以戴上，走动一下，看看戴在手腕上的感觉如何，并短暂地走到外面，在自然光下观察它。店员同意了，并说：“我知道像您这样的人，我可以放心地把商品交给您。”该顾客戴着手表走出了商店，并且没有回来。一周后，店员在一次聚会上发现该顾客正戴着那块手表。她告诉他，他必须要么付钱买下手表，要么把它还回来。他恶狠狠地说：“你要是惹我，你会后悔的。”店员受到恐吓，便退缩了。

以下罪行列表按严重程度降序排列。

该顾客所犯的最严重的罪行是什么？

zh-choices.A: 抢劫罪。
zh-choices.B: 盗窃罪。
zh-choices.C: 诈骗罪。
zh-choices.D: 侵占罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：盗窃罪（larceny）里“先用虚假陈述骗到的是占有还是所有权”，以及后续威胁能不能把前面的取走行为变成抢劫（robbery）。

三秒认题路径：

虚假冒充 → 骗到占有 → 带走并据为己有 → 先成立 larceny → 后威胁不改性

核心法律规则

盗窃（larceny）要求：未经同意、擅自拿走并搬运他人动产，再加上永久剥夺意图。考场意思：你不是只“摸了一下”，而是把东西拿离原处并想据为己有。

如果同意是靠故意虚假陈述骗来的，同意（consent）就是无效的；题目里这就是 larceny by trick。考场意思：表面上对方让你拿，实质上法上没真同意。

抢劫（robbery）是在盗窃基础上，再用暴力或胁迫从被害人本人或在场范围内夺取。考场意思：必须是“带着威胁去拿”，不是“先偷走，后来才吓人”。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用；本题锁定的是财产犯罪分类。这里的关键是骗取占有后带走，构成 larceny by trick。

思维导图

先看这是不是 拿走他人财物 的题？
是：客户把表拿出店、想永久留下 → 先看 larceny。
同意从哪来？
被害人是被“我是谁”骗到才同意 → known misrepresentation 让同意无效。
结论：骗到的是占有（possession），不是所有权 → larceny by trick。
再问：后来的威胁能把案子改成 robbery 吗？
不能，因为“先拿走”已经完成，后面的“you'll be sorry”只是追回时的威胁，不是取走时的强迫。
所以最重罪名仍是 B. 盗窃（larceny）。
对照：false pretenses 需要骗到的是所有权（title）；embezzlement 需要先合法占有。
本题都没到：客户只是靠谎话拿到表的占有，不是 title，也不是 lawful possession。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他后来用威胁逼退店员，所以像抢劫（robbery）。

但考试真正问的是：取走那一刻有没有暴力或胁迫；这里先靠谎言拿到表，后威胁只是事后加戏。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

你也可能会把它看成 false pretenses，但那题型要求骗到的是title；本题只骗到可携带的占有。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 假冒市长之子 让店员无效同意，客户骗到的是占有并带走手表，正是 larceny by trick。

❌ 法律适用 | 胁迫时点误判

✕ A: 把事后威胁当成取走时暴力，robbery 的时点错了。

❌ 概念混淆 | title占有偷换

✕ C: 以为骗到的是 title，其实只是临时占有。

❌ 事实误判 | 合法占有缺失

✕ D: 先有合法保管再挪用的前提没有，embezzlement 不成立。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清骗到的是占有还是所有权，再看暴力是否发生在取走当时。

考场速记

记忆口诀：骗占有是 larceny by trick，骗 title 是 false pretenses，先合法占有再挪用是 embezzlement，拿的时候有暴力才是 robbery。

这题一眼抓住“假身份骗同意 + 先拿走再威胁”，基本就能秒选 B。

reason.zh: 表明同意是由欺诈诱导的，指向以欺骗手段进行的盗窃罪。

reason.zh: 错误，因为受害者仅转移了手表的保管权，而非所有权。

reason.en: Incorrect because the customer was never in lawful possession of the watch.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A woman and her partner robbed a bank. Although they split the money they had stolen in half, the woman became greedy and decided to steal the partner's share. The woman knew that the partner had stashed his share of the money in a house that had been abandoned for some time. She decided to sneak into the house at night and steal the money. That night, the woman went to the back door of the house, and when she tried the doorknob, she discovered that it was unlocked. She snuck into the house, walked around until she found the partner's money in one of the rooms, and took it. A neighbor heard the woman rummaging in the house and immediately called the police. The police tracked the woman down and arrested her for burglary.
In a jurisdiction that follows the common law with respect to criminal offenses, is the woman guilty of burglary?

choices.A: No, because the back door to the house was unlocked.
choices.B: No, because the house was abandoned.
choices.C: Yes, because the woman intended to permanently deprive the partner of the money.
choices.D: Yes, because the woman used force to enter the house.

questions.explanation:
Dwelling requirement for common-law burglary

Common-law burglary is the unlawful breaking and entering of another's dwelling at night with the specific intent to commit a felony therein. A dwelling is defined as a structure regularly occupied for habitation. Although the structure need not be occupied at the time of the breaking, it must not be abandoned. That is because common-law burglary seeks only to protect a person's right of habitation.

Here, the woman broke into the house at night with the specific intent to steal the partner's money (ie, to commit larceny) (Choice C). However, the house was abandoned when she broke in. As a result, the house does not constitute a dwelling for purposes of a common-law burglary, and the woman is not guilty of this crime.

(Choices A & D) A breaking can be accomplished by using even slight force, such as opening an unlocked door (as seen here). However, walking through an already open door would not constitute a breaking.

📌 Educational Objective

For common-law burglary, a dwelling is defined as a structure regularly occupied for habitation. Although the structure need not be occupied at the time of the breaking, it must not be abandoned.

📚 References
  • Wayne R. LaFave, 3 Substantive Criminal Law § 21.1(c) (3d ed. 2020) (defining "dwelling of another").
questions.zh-question:
一名女子和她的同伙抢劫了一家银行。尽管他们将偷来的钱平分，但该女子变得贪婪，决定偷走同伙的那一份。该女子知道同伙把他的那份钱藏在了一栋废弃已久的房子里。她决定在晚上潜入这栋房子偷走那笔钱。那天晚上，该女子走到房子的后门，当她试着转动门把手时，发现门没有锁。她潜入房子，四处走动，直到在一个房间里找到了同伙的钱，并拿走了它。一位邻居听到该女子在房子里翻找的声音，立即报了警。警方追查到该女子，并以入室犯法罪 (burglary) 逮捕了她。

在一个遵循普通法 (common law) 处理刑事犯罪的司法管辖区内，该女子是否犯有入室犯法罪 (burglary)？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为房子的后门没有上锁。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该房屋已被废弃。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为该女子意图永久剥夺其同伙对钱财的所有权。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该女子使用了暴力进入该房屋。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Other Crimes - Crimes against property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：普通法 burglary 里的 dwelling（住宅） 必须是仍用于居住的房屋，abandoned（已废弃） 的房子不算，所以进去了也不构成 burglary。

三秒认题路径：

夜里进去 → 先看 dwelling → 再看是否 abandoned → 废弃房 → 不成立

核心法律规则

普通法 burglary（入室盗窃） 需要：夜间、breaking and entering（破门而入）、进入他人 dwelling（住宅），并且带着实施重罪的特定故意。这里的 dwelling 考场意思：必须是“通常拿来住人”的地方。房子就算当时没人，也可以是 dwelling；但如果已经 abandoned（废弃），就不是 dwelling 了。所以上诉式记忆不是盯着“有没有锁”“有没有进去”，而是先问“这房子还算不算家”。

核心判例：普通法 burglary 的 dwelling 规则，关键就在“通常用于居住”而不是“当时有没有人在屋里”；废弃房屋不满足 dwelling 要件，所以不能成立 burglary。

思维导图

先问：这是不是普通法 burglary？
第一关夜里进入他人房屋 → 继续看是不是 dwelling（住宅）。
第二关房屋是否“通常用于居住”？
YES没人住也可以，只要还保留住宅属性 → 可能成立 burglary。
NO若已 abandoned（废弃） → 卡死：不是 dwelling，burglary 直接出局
本题落点她确实夜里进去，也想偷钱，但房子已废弃 → 答案：No。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她夜里翻窗进门，还偷了钱，所以应该就是 burglary。
但考试真正问的是：这栋房子到底还是不是 dwelling（住宅），不是她有没有偷心。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这里真正卡点是房屋已经废弃，dwelling 要件没过。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干关键事实是房子已 abandoned；普通法 burglary 只保护仍有居住属性的 dwelling，所以她虽夜里进去并想偷钱，仍不成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 开门误当无破门

✕ A: 盯着 unlocked 就以为没 breaking。

❌ 法律适用 | 盗意套错要件

✕ C: 把她的偷钱目的当成能补回 dwelling 要件。

❌ 事实误判 | 轻微用力夸大

✕ D: 把 used force 说成关键，其实入口是否锁着不救废弃房。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓 dwelling，再看 abandoned；只要房屋已废弃，后面的进入方式和盗意都救不回来。

考场速记

记住一句：普通法 burglary 先看 dwelling（住宅），再看夜间进入和盗意；房子已经废弃，就直接不是 burglary。以后见到“空屋、废屋、弃屋”，先把“dwelling”从脑中划掉。

reason.zh: 指明了盗窃意图，但忽略了缺失的住宅要素。

reason.zh: 错误地暗示需要实际暴力或者使用了暴力。

highlights.text: at night

reason.en: Satisfies the common law temporal element of burglary.
reason.zh: 满足普通法入室盗窃的夜间时间要素。

highlights.text: common law with respect to criminal offenses

reason.en: Directs the analysis to strict common law rules.

highlights.text: is the woman guilty of burglary

reason.en: Defines the core legal question to resolve.
reason.zh: 明确了核心待决法律问题。
